explanation: 该论文的主题是关于墨西哥在REDD+（减少毁林和森林退化）方面的学术文献综述，而非大气环境遥感技术，如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析或气溶胶反演。因此，它与大气环境遥感技术没有强关联。
authors: Jovanka Špirić;María Liliana Ávalos-Rodríguez;Edgar Gregorio Leija-Loredo
title: Systematic mapping of academic literature on REDD+ in Mexico: research gaps and ways forward
abstract: Academic literature has extensively analyzed REDD+, with some studies criticizing its effectiveness, efficiency, and equity, and others proposing recommendations to improve implementation and outcomes. Mexico was among the pioneering countries in REDD+ implementation, introducing legislative reforms (2008), launching pilot initiatives (2011–2015), and publishing its national REDD+ strategy (2017). However, the country did not progress toward the performance-based payment phase as planned. Despite substantial scholarly attention and several topical review articles, no systematic review of academic literature on REDD+ has focused exclusively on Mexico. This study addresses this gap through a systematic mapping of the scientific literature on REDD+ in Mexico. The objectives were to identify thematic and methodological research gaps, systematize policy and practice recommendations, and assess the feasibility of conducting a full systematic review or a meta-analysis. Our findings on the evolution and geographic distribution of REDD+ studies indicate a link between national policy processes and implementation dynamics that may have generated research opportunities through pilot activities, institutional collaborations, and funding. Among ten broad topics, three dominated the literature: carbon estimation and assessment, environmental governance, and public policies design. Carbon estimation and assessment studies are largely quantitative; however, the feasibility of meta-analysis is constrained by inconsistent reporting and the absence of standardized outcome indicators. In contrast, governance and public policies studies are predominantly qualitative and exploratory or descriptive. Longitudinal and evaluative studies remain scarce, and the lack of standardized social indicators limits systematic cross-case comparison and assessment of institutional change over time. Overall, the trajectory of REDD+ research in Mexico reflects broader trends in environmental governance scholarship, moving from an initial focus on institutional design and participation toward greater attention to impact evaluation. The existing academic literature on REDD+ in Mexico provides a rich but methodologically heterogeneous evidence, suitable for qualitative synthesis but still insufficiently standardized for rigorous meta-analysis.

explanation: 该论文研究的是Da Qi-1 ACDL卫星对XCO2（二氧化碳柱平均干空气摩尔分数）的遥感测量，并与被动卫星（如OCO-2、OCO-3、GOSAT）的产品一致性进行比较，这直接涉及大气环境遥感技术，特别是大气成分分析和卫星观测。
authors: Yike Wang;Ge Han;Hongyuan Zhang;Yiyang Huang;Kangjie Zhou;Wei Gong
title: Assessing the consistency of XCO2 products from DQ-1 ACDL and passive satellites using a unified comparison framework
abstract:
This study establishes a unified framework to assess the consistency of DQ-1 (Da Qi-1) ACDL (Aerosol and Carbon Dioxide Lidar) XCO2 with passive satellite products while considering sampling and column-definition differences. DQ-1 agrees well with TCCON (Total Carbon Column Observing Network) and shows consistent spatial patterns with OCO-2, OCO-3 (Orbiting Carbon Observatory), GOSAT, and GOSAT-2 (Greenhouse gases Observing SATellite) over selected regions. It provides complementary XCO2 observations where passive measurements are limited, including nighttime and high latitudes, supporting future joint carbon monitoring and inversion studies. 
 Da Qi-1 (DQ-1) carries the Aerosol and Carbon Dioxide Lidar (ACDL), a spaceborne integrated path differential absorption (IPDA) lidar that retrieves the column-averaged dry-air mole fraction of carbon dioxide (XCO2)  using active laser measurements. Unlike passive near-infrared/shortwave-infrared sensors that rely on reflected sunlight, ACDL can observe at night and high latitudes, but its sampling and effective column definition differ from passive XCO2 products. Evaluation is therefore needed before active and passive observations can be interpreted jointly. We compare DQ-1 ACDL with the Orbiting Carbon Observatory (OCO-2 and OCO-3) and Greenhouse gases Observing SATellite (GOSAT and GOSAT-2) missions from June 2022–December 2024 using a unified framework that combines Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS)-based coherence assessment, sampling availability, daily 2° aggregation, spatiotemporal collocation, and correction for XCO2 column-definition differences. Validation against the Total Carbon Column Observing Network (TCCON) gives R=0.92, a mean bias of 0.21 ppm, and a root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 1.49 ppm for daytime DQ-1, comparable to GOSAT. Over coherent and well-sampled regions, DQ-1 is broadly consistent with OCO-2 and OCO-3, with mean differences generally below 0.5 ppm and similar spatial and meridional structures. Over ocean, the DQ-1–OCO differences vary with surface reflectance and wind speed, with different reflectance relationships for OCO-2 and OCO-3. Nighttime DQ-1 is also broadly consistent with CAMS-derived XCO2. Regional analyses show complementary DQ-1 coverage where passive observations are limited. These results support DQ-1 ACDL as a quantitatively comparable and complementary component of the satellite XCO2 observing system.

explanation: 该论文研究了GHGSat卫星星座对甲烷泄漏的探测和量化性能，涉及卫星遥感技术、大气成分分析和空气质量监测，与大气环境遥感技术密切相关。
authors: Antoine Ramier;Hanford Deglint;Ariane Deslieres;Lia Formenti;Marianne Girard;Dylan Jervis;David J. Marshall;Jean-Philippe W. MacLean;Jason McKeever;Andrew McKell;Mathias Strupler;Ewan Tarrant
title: Performance validation of the GHGSat methane constellation via controlled releases
abstract:
We validated the GHGSat fleet against a large set of precisely measured emissions from 2021 to 2026 and built a model linking detection probability to leak rate, wind, retrieval noise, and resolution. In typical conditions the satellites detect a leak of about 100 kilograms per hour half the time and quantify its rate accurately. This sets a clear benchmark for how reliably satellites detect and measure methane leaks, which is essential for trustworthy emissions reporting and mitigation. 
 Satellite remote sensing has become an important tool for detecting, quantifying, and attributing methane emissions, yet a rigorous, condition-dependent characterization of point-source imager performance validated against controlled releases with known emission rates remains limited, despite being essential to support its use in regulatory and voluntary reporting frameworks. We present a comprehensive performance assessment of the GHGSat constellation of high-resolution methane-imaging satellites based on a multi-campaign controlled release dataset spanning 2021 to 2026 that combines self-organized campaigns with independent third-party experiments. We develop a probabilistic, environmental conditions-dependent detection model in which the probability of detection depends on the plume signal to noise ratio (SNR), which is in turn a function of emission rate, wind speed, retrieval noise, and spatial resolution. Comparing model variants over subsets of these predictors, we find that emission rate, wind speed, and retrieval noise are the dominant drivers of detection, while spatial resolution improves the fit only when combined with the others. We find that an SNR of 1.72 ± 0.39 is required to achieve a 50 % probability of detection, which translates to a detection limit Q50 = 99.0 ± 5.3 kg h−1 in median environmental conditions encountered in controlled releases (3 m s−1 wind speed, 7 mmol m−2 column density noise, 27 m resolution). Evaluated over global observing conditions, the same model gives a median Q50= 159.7 kg h−1. The estimated Q50 is shown to converge stably as data accumulate and to remain consistent when blind validation samples are added to self-organized releases. Quantification accuracy is evaluated through parity analysis of estimated versus metered emission rates, yielding an ordinary least squares slope of 0.93 ± 0.03 and R2 of 0.92 using reported model winds, improving to 0.98 ± 0.03 and R2= 0.93 with a co-located anemometer wind adjusted to a 10 m reference height. A comparison of emission rate estimates based on ERA5, IFS, and HRRR winds shows that quantification accuracy metrics derived from this dataset were largely insensitive to the choice of operationally available wind product, with a residual underestimation at low emission rates that correlates with wind model spatial resolution. We further demonstrate a bias correction combining a local concentration background correction with an empirically recalibrated effective wind speed, which recovers the low-rate sources that were previously underestimated and removes most of the residual bias without degrading accuracy at higher emission rates. These results establish a transparent, statistically grounded baseline for the GHGSat constellation's detection and quantification performance and provide a methodological framework that can be extended as additional controlled-release data become available.

explanation: 该论文研究的是韩国济州岛降水中的稳定水同位素数据，包括δ18O和δ2H的测量值，以及与气温、降水量的相关性。这些数据可用于分析大气成分和水分循环，与大气环境遥感技术中的空气质量和大气成分分析相关。
authors: Kwang-Sik Lee;Dong-Chan Koh;Young-Hee Kim;Won-Bae Park;Songyi Kim;Hyejung Jung;Yeon-Sik Bong;Woo-Jin Shin;Chaeyoung Kim;Jeonghoon Lee
title: A spatially resolved dataset of stable water isotopes in monthly precipitation over Jeju Island, Korea (2000–2003)
abstract:
We present 462 paired measurements of stable oxygen and hydrogen isotopes in monthly precipitation from 15 sites on Jeju Island, South Korea, collected between 2000 and 2003. Isotope values were generally lower in summer and decreased with elevation. Published with weather data and sampling information, this historical dataset provides a baseline for future monitoring and supports research on groundwater recharge and the island’s water cycle. 
 Spatially resolved, multi-year observations of stable water isotopes in precipitation remain scarce for high-relief maritime islands. We present a historical dataset of monthly precipitation isotopes collected between September 2000 and December 2003 at 15 stations on Jeju Island, South Korea, spanning elevations of 5–1230 ma.s.l. The dataset contains 462 paired δ18O and δ2H measurements, deuterium excess (d-excess = δ2H − 8 × δ18O), station and sampling metadata, and 488 station-month records of precipitation and air-temperature estimates, including 26 records without corresponding isotope measurements. Missing isotope observations were not imputed. Individual δ18O and δ2H values range from −13.2 ‰ to −2.0 ‰ and from −93.3 ‰ to −5.8 ‰, respectively, and generally exhibit lower values in summer than during the cool season. Unweighted station means for the common 2002–2003 period yield elevation gradients of −0.146 ± 0.013 ‰ per 100 m for δ18O and −1.043 ± 0.128 ‰ per 100 m for δ2H, with uncertainties expressed as standard errors. An island–nearshore comparison with isotope-enabled model output provides context for broad seasonal variability. By recovering and openly publishing observations collected more than two decades ago, this dataset preserves a historical baseline for subsequent precipitation-isotope monitoring and hydrological studies on Jeju Island. The data are available at https://doi.org/10.22747/paper_data.20260219.42 (Lee et al., 2026).

explanation: 该论文主要关注城市树木的细粒度分类，利用图像数据集支持城市规划和管理，与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析、气溶胶反演）关联性较弱。
authors: Jiapeng Li;Yingjing Huang;Fan Zhang;Shengli Tao;Zhen Dong;Jun Yang;Yu Liu
title: ArborVerse: Scaling Fine-Grained Urban Tree Species Classification to Millions of Trees Worldwide
abstract:
Street trees make cities healthier and more livable, but global research has been limited by scarce shared data. We created StreetTree, a public collection of over 12 million street-level images covering more than 8,300 tree species in 133 countries. Tests show that current image classification methods still struggle with real street scenes, where trees can look alike, change with seasons, and appear in varied conditions. StreetTree can support tree mapping, planning and greener city management. 
 The fine-grained classification of street trees is a crucial task for urban planning, streetscape management, and the assessment of urban ecosystem services. However, progress in this field has been hindered by the lack of large-scale, geographically diverse, and publicly available benchmark datasets specifically designed for street trees. To address this critical gap, we introduce StreetTree, the world’s first large-scale benchmark dataset dedicated to fine-grained street tree classification. The dataset contains over 12 million images covering more than 8,300 common street tree species, collected from urban streetscapes across 133 countries spanning five continents, and supplemented with expert-verified observational data. StreetTree poses challenges for pretrained vision models under complex urban environments: high inter-species visual similarity, long-tailed natural distributions, significant intra-class variations caused by seasonal changes, and diverse imaging conditions such as lighting, occlusions from buildings, and varying camera angles. In addition, we provide a hierarchical taxonomy (order–family–genus–species) to support research in hierarchical classification and representation learning. Through extensive experiments with various vision models, we establish solid baselines and reveal the limitations of existing methods in handling such real-world complexities. We believe that StreetTree will serve as a key resource for driving new advancements at the intersection of computer vision and urban science. The data is now publicly available at https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.32172486 (Li et al., 2026).

explanation: 该论文研究的是渤海海域和入海河流沉积物中的植物花粉和孢子，旨在通过这些数据解读过去景观和气候变化。虽然涉及海洋和河流环境，但主要关注的是花粉和孢子的分布及其与气候、地理环境的关系，而非大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析或气溶胶反演等）。因此，它与大气环境遥感技术的关联性不强。
authors: Jie Li;Shixiong Yang;Siyuan Ye;Xiangjun Meng;Xiaohui Chen;Xi Mei;Maosheng Gao;Qian Hao;Xianyong Cao;Bin Chen;Sangheon Yi;Guangming Zhao
title: A paired marine-fluvial modern pollen dataset from the Bohai Sea and its inflowing rivers, China
abstract:
To better read past landscape and climate changes from seafloor sediments, we built a paired record of plant pollen and spores from 430 Bohai Sea samples and 104 river samples from 16 rivers. The results show that pine pollen is more common in deeper, offshore areas, while grasses and salt-tolerant plants are more common near coasts and river mouths. This open dataset helps researchers judge how rivers, wind, and water depth shape the plant signals preserved in sea sediments. 
 Modern marine pollen records can be interpreted reliably only when the main source-to-sink processes between terrestrial vegetation, rivers, and marine depocentres are documented by comparable modern data. Here, we present and quality-assess a paired marine-fluvial pollen dataset for the Bohai Sea, China, consisting of 430 marine surface-sediment samples and 104 fluvial surface-sediment samples from 16 major inflowing rivers. The dataset includes sample coordinates, water depth for marine stations, river and regional identifiers, pollen and spore counts and percentages, pollen concentrations, and grain-size parameters. In total, 104 pollen and spore morphotypes were identified. Marine assemblages are dominated by arboreal pollen, especially Pinus (mean 59 %), whereas nearshore and river-influenced settings contain higher proportions of herbaceous taxa, particularly Chenopodiaceae/Amaranthaceae-type (mean 14 %), Artemisia, and Poaceae. Redundancy analysis after variance-inflation-factor screening indicates that water depth is the strongest retained predictor of marine pollen composition (λ1/λ2=0.303), followed by geographic position and sediment texture. In river samples, geographic position, water discharge, and pollen concentration together explain 20.53 % of the compositional variance. Along the 0–35 m depth interval, arboreal pollen and Pinus percentages increase with water depth, whereas herbaceous percentages decrease, providing an internally consistent modern analogue for distinguishing nearshore fluvial influence from more distal marine influence, where buoyant saccate pollen is enriched by a combination of atmospheric transport and hydrodynamic sorting. The dataset is intended primarily as a reusable calibration and quality-assessment resource for palaeoenvironmental studies in the Bohai-Yellow Sea region. The archived data are available at the National Tibetan Plateau Data Center (TPDC; https://doi.org/10.11888/Paleoenv.tpdc.303516, Li and Yang, 2026).

explanation: 该论文主要研究的是全球重力场的解决方案，虽然涉及卫星数据、海洋学应用等，但与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析、气溶胶反演）关系不大，因此不 strongly related。
authors: Jianhao Xuan;Qiujie Chen;Yunzhong Shen;Xingfu Zhang;Yun Xiao
title: Tongji-GMMG2025C: A High-Resolution Global Gravity Field Solution Integrated from Heterogeneous Gravity Data via a Grid-based VCE Method
abstract:
We developed a new high-resolution global gravity field model by integrating satellite, marine, terrestrial, airborne, polar, and topographic gravity information. The model substantially improves gravity estimation accuracy in coastal, polar, and data-sparse regions. Accuracy improves by 9 %–24 % within 10 km of the coastline and by approximately 40 % over Antarctica. The dataset can be used for geodesy, oceanography, and other Earth science applications. 
 In this study, we present Tongji-GMMG2025C, a high-resolution global gravity field solution complete to degree and order (d/o) 2190. The solution combines GRACE and GOCE satellite gravity information with five marine gravity datasets derived from satellite altimetry, four topographic gravity field models, pseudo terrestrial observations generated from EGM2008 up to d/o 719, high-resolution Antarctic gravity anomaly grids (AntGG2021), and Arctic Gravity Project (ArcGP) datasets. Grid-level variance component estimation (VCE) is used to combine the marine and topographic datasets separately. The Tongji-GMMG2021S satellite-based full normal equation system is then combined with a terrestrial block-diagonal normal equation derived from global 5’×5’ gravity anomaly grids. As a multi-source integrated solution, Tongji-GMMG2025C demonstrates lower residual statistics than single-source based solutions, exhibiting improvements of 0.01~0.21 mGal in measured free-air gravity anomalies and shipborne gravity anomaly enhancements of 0.08~0.54 mGal. Comparison with other existing gravity field solutions EGM2008, EIGEN-6C4, SGG-UGM-2, and XGM2019e reveals a good performance of our new combination solution Tongji-GMMG2025C and the closest agreement with XGM2019e. In oceanographic applications, Tongji-GMMG2025C achieves a root mean square error (RMSE) of 75.27 cm/s in geostrophic current determination relative to the DTU22MDT, outperforming EIGEN-6C4 by over 4.87 cm/s. Continental geoid evaluations in data-sparse regions yield accuracies of 38.94 cm (surrounding Brazil), 34.45 cm (surrounding Africa), and 50.60 cm (surrounding India), representing a 24 % improvement over EGM2008 in the surrounding Brazil region. Validation against millions of shipborne gravity measurements indicates that Tongji-GMMG2025C performs favourably, particularly in the 0~10 km coastal zone, where it achieves an accuracy of 6.99 mGal, outperforming existing models by 9 % to 24 %. Similarly, the model establishes an accuracy improvement of approximately 40 % compared to EGM2008 over Antarctica. These results demonstrate that Tongji-GMMG2025C may provide useful complementary gravity information in data-sparse regions. The Tongji-GMMG2025C solution is available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22667828 (Xuan et al., 2026).

explanation: 该论文与大气环境遥感技术密切相关，因为它涉及野火事件的数据库构建，野火是大气环境中的一个重要因素，其监测和研究对于空气质量、大气成分分析等具有重要意义。
authors: Eric S. Kasischke;Nancy H. French
title: An integrated wildfire event database for improved fire science research for the continental United States, 1992–2021
abstract:
A new wildfire event dataset was developed to improve information for studying wildfires in the continental United State for 1992 to 2021. It was created by integrating data from three existing datasets with information obtained from regional reports and datasets and reports found on the world wide web. For all United States regions, calculations using this new dataset increases total burned area, as well as the number of and burned  area in extreme wildfires (those larger than 5000 hectares). 
 This paper describes a wildfire event dataset that was initially created by mining information from three existing national datasets that have provided the foundation for numerous wildfire studies in the continental United States over the past two decades. The goal for creating this dataset was to address existing uncertainties and ambiguities in the the existing datasets by using information from regional reports and datasets and searches of the world wide web. Wildfire events not contained in the three datasets were added as new records. Approaches were developed to harvest information for records where there were significant differences in the size of the same fire from different datasets. Specific attention was paid to fires named as complexes, those contained multiple fires, smaller events that had merged to form larger events, events that had joined, events where the size was incorrectly reported, and duplicate events. This new wildfire event dataset provides more accurate information on the number and sizes of individual wildfires and improved information for quantifying annual area burned and changes in extreme wildfire activity over a three-decade period (1992 to 2021) at different spatial scales. Results are presented that illustrate the differences in wildfire characteristics developed from the new dataset and those currently being used by the fire science community.

explanation: 该论文使用多传感器卫星观测数据（如MODIS、VIIRS和OLCI）开发了一个关于中国边缘海域漂浮大型藻类（如Ulva prolifera和Sargassum horneri）的周度数据集，涉及了藻华的监测、季节性模式、年际变化和快速动态，这与大气环境遥感技术中的空气质量监测、卫星观测和大气成分分析等领域密切相关。
authors: Mingqing Liu;Zhaotong Chen;Yingcheng Lu;Qianguo Xing;Jiaochan Hu;Haoyang Yu;Zhongbin B. Li;Mengqiu Wang
title: A 1-km weekly dataset of floating Ulva prolifera and Sargassum horneri blooms in China’s marginal seas derived from multi-sensor satellite observations
abstract:
Floating macroalgal blooms in China’s coastal seas can rapidly expand and spread, affecting marine ecosystems and human activities. This study developed a weekly dataset of two major floating macroalgae species from 2018 to 2025 using observations from multiple satellites. The dataset captures seasonal patterns, yearly changes, and rapid bloom dynamics, providing a consistent resource for understanding bloom development and supporting coastal monitoring. 
 Floating macroalgae blooms, primarily caused by Ulva prolifera and Sargassum horneri, frequently occur in the marginal seas around China, posing significant ecological and economic challenges.  However, a long-term, high-frequency monitoring dataset capable of capturing bloom seasonality, interannual variability, and rapid transport dynamics across multiple sea regions remains limited.  In this study, we derived 1-km weekly mean U. prolifera and S. horneri dataset covering 2018 to 2025, generated from 85,868 multi-sensor satellite images acquired from the Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS), Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS), and Ocean and Land Colour Instrument (OLCI).  By integrating complementary observations from multiple satellite sensors, the dataset substantially improves temporal continuity and observation availability relative to single-sensor products, enabling more complete characterization of rapidly evolving macroalgal blooms.  A two-step deep learning-based approach was employed to detect and distinguish U. prolifera and S. horneri, achieving >90% accuracy for both bloom extraction and species classification across sensors.  Independent validation using hyperspectral Plankton, Aerosol, Cloud, ocean Ecosystem (PACE) Ocean Color Instrument (OCI) and Sentinel-2 MultiSpectral Instrument (MSI) data further supports the reliability of species discrimination.  The pair-wise cross-sensor biomass comparisons show strong consistency, with R² > 0.8 for both species.  The dataset reveals distinct spatiotemporal patterns of the two macroalgal species.  U. prolifera blooms in the Yellow Sea exhibit a relatively consistent seasonal cycle from May to August, with rapid aggregation and dissipation and the highest biomass recorded in 2021, whereas S. horneri shows a broader and more variable distribution across the East China Sea, with record-high biomass observed in 2024.  Weekly observations further resolve rapid bloom aggregation, transport, and dissipation processes that are difficult to capture using monthly composites.  Weekly products provide a balance between temporal resolution and observational completeness, preserving short-term bloom variability while supporting consistent interannual comparisons.  Compared with weekly products, monthly composites underestimated seasonal peak biomass by 24–50% for S. horneri and 12–52% for U. prolifera during 2018–2025.  In contrast, daily products were more sensitive to short-term biomass fluctuations, which could alter the identification of the year with the highest boom intensity, highlighting the importance of temporal aggregation for robust interannual comparisons.  Comparisons with previous studies and reported bloom events demonstrate that the dataset reliably reproduces observed spatial distributions and seasonal characteristics.  By providing a high-resolution, weekly, and species-resolved dataset of floating macroalgae, this study offers a consistent observational foundation for investigating species-specific bloom dynamics, assessing their responses to environmental variability, and enabling data-driven management and early warning of macroalgal blooms in China’s marginal seas.

explanation: 该论文研究的是多频段卫星土壤湿度数据的协同同化方案，涉及卫星观测、数据融合和同化技术，与大气环境遥感技术（如卫星观测、大气成分分析）密切相关。
authors: Xuesong Bai;Zhaohui Lin;Zhengkun Qin;Juan Li
title: A preliminary study on a synergistic assimilation scheme for multi-band satellite soil moisture data
abstract:
Accurate soil moisture data is essential for predicting weather. This study examined how observations from three satellites can be combined to improve land-surface simulations. While each satellite helps, their value changes with vegetation type. Merging these data sources gives a more reliable estimate of soil wetness, especially in central and western China. This approach strengthens soil-water monitoring and supports more dependable climate forecasting. 
 Soil moisture retrievals from satellite sensors operating at different microwave frequencies provide diverse and complementary data sources for assimilation. However, fully exploiting the advantages of each frequency band while increasing the volume of assimilated observations remains a challenge. This study assimilates soil-moisture retrievals from three dominant-frequency instruments – SMAP (Soil Moisture Active–Passive), ASCAT (Advanced Scatterometer), and MWRI (Microwave Radiation Imager) – into the Common Land Model (CoLM) via the Simplified Extended Kalman Filter (SEKF). Based on the systematic assessment of the disparate impacts of each single-band product, we propose and test a synergistic multi-satellite assimilation framework that optimally combines the complementary information inherent in the multi-frequency observations. Results show that assimilating soil-moisture retrievals improves the accuracy of the CoLM land-surface model; nevertheless, the effectiveness of each product varies with vegetation type. Analyses of simultaneous multi-source assimilation indicate that retrieval uncertainties associated with frequency-dependent differences in vegetation penetration capability are the dominant factor controlling the effectiveness of joint assimilation. When SMAP and ASCAT products are already ingested, the additional introduction of MWRI data over low-stature vegetation, where vegetation attenuation is relatively weak, provides complementary information and further enhances the joint assimilation performance. Validation against in-situ observations across China demonstrates that the largest improvements occur in the central and western parts of the country: compared with the open-loop simulation, the domain-mean correlation coefficient rises by about 0.25, while the error declines from 0.068 to 0.058 m3 m−3. This indicates that improvements from multi-sensor assimilation stem not only from increased data volume but also from the complementary characteristics of the assimilated products. These findings provide valuable insights into the design of synergistic multi-sensor land data assimilation systems and contribute to improving land surface modeling, as well as weather and climate prediction accuracy.

explanation: 该论文与大气环境遥感技术密切相关，因为它涉及使用化学传输模型（CTMs）和化学气候模型（CCMs）来研究地面臭氧、颗粒物（PM）、氮和硫沉降的长程传输及其影响。这些模型用于分析不同全球区域的污染移动和来源贡献，为改进空气质量政策提供科学依据，这与大气成分分析和空气质量监测直接相关。
authors: Tim Butler;Tabish Ansari;Claudio A. Belis;Elisa Bergas-Masso;Willem van Caspel;Hilde Fagerli;Johannes Flemming;Marta Garcia Vivanco;Paul Griffiths;Douglas S. Hamilton;Coralina Hernandez Trujillo;Lena Höglund-Isaksson;Vincent Huijnen;Johannes W. Kaiser;Gerbrand Koren;Zbigniew Klimont;Florian Lindl;Aura Lupascu;Mariano Mertens;Martijn Schaap;Steven T. Turnock;Oliver Wild;Philipp Weiss;Jacek Kaminski;Rosa Wu;Terry Keating
title: HTAP3-OPNS: ozone, PM, nitrogen and sulphur deposition – multi-model experiments to support the revision of the CLRTAP Gothenburg Protocol
abstract:
Air pollution travels across continents, meaning emissions in one region can affect air quality far away. To better understand this, scientists from many groups are planning to run coordinated computer simulations of the atmosphere. By comparing results across models and emission scenarios, the planned study will show how pollution moves between regions and which sources matter most, helping governments design more effective air quality policies. 
 HTAP3-OPNS is a multi-model exercise designed to support the revision of the Gothenburg Protocol under the UNECE Convention on Long-Range Transboundary Air Pollution (CLRTAP). Using an ensemble of Chemical Transport Models (CTMs) and Chemistry-Climate Models (CCMs), this study investigates the long-range transport and impacts of ground-level ozone, particulate matter (PM), and nitrogen and sulphur deposition across different global regions. The project aims to assess the contributions of regional versus extra-regional emission sources, evaluate the suitability of current models, and project changes in air pollution under future emission scenarios and climate conditions. A series of perturbation simulations will enable the development of an ensemble emulator to explore and evaluate potential mitigation strategies efficiently. This paper outlines the scientific and policy questions motivating the study, describes the experimental design, including input datasets, model configurations, and required outputs, and discusses methodologies for data handling and analysis. The results will provide crucial insights for policy decisions aiming to improve air quality, protect human health, and protect ecosystems worldwide.

authors: Peter Köhler;Stefan Mulitza
title: Net Carbon Transfer From Ocean to Land During the Last Deglaciation Synchronous With Sea Level Rise and Lagging Atmospheric CO2 by Several Millennia
abstract: The sequence of events in the global carbon cycle during deglaciations is not entirely understood. Here, we analyze mean ocean δ13 ${\delta }^{13}$C and δ18 ${\delta }^{18}$O in an updated compilation of foraminiferal stable isotope data comprising 902 time series from 381 sediment cores, with individual records covering intervals within the past 23,000 years. We use changes in mean ocean temperature from ice cores to split δ18 ${\delta }^{18}$O into its temperature and seawater components. We show that a 0.48±0.05 $0.48\pm 0.05$‰ rise in mean ocean δ13 ${\delta }^{13}$C occurred quasi‐synchronously with changes in seawater δ18 ${\delta }^{18}$O and is lagging the rise in atmospheric CO2 ${\mathrm{C}\mathrm{O}}_{2}$ during Termination I by ∼2,000 years. Since mean ocean δ13 ${\delta }^{13}$C is understood to mainly record net changes in land carbon storage and seawater δ18 ${\delta }^{18}$O is mainly depicting the rise in global mean sea level this implies that land carbon changed in‐phase with sea level and not with atmospheric CO2 ${\mathrm{C}\mathrm{O}}_{2}$.

authors: Flavio Petricca;Dustin Buccino
title: A Radio Science Experiment for Dragonfly to Investigate Titan's Rotation and Interior Structure
abstract: NASA's mission Dragonfly to Titan is scheduled for launch in 2028 with arrival in 2034 to study Titan's prebiotic chemistry and habitability. We propose a radio science experiment for Dragonfly, in which radiometric tracking of the rotorcraft from the Deep Space Network, already baselined for communications and navigation, is used as a precision geodetic instrument to measure Titan's rotational state and tidal deformations, without any modification to the spacecraft. We perform simulations of the experiment and compute its expected performances in terms of the uncertainties on the retrieved geophysical parameters. Our results indicate that the rotation and tidal parameters can be retrieved with outstanding precision, sufficient to discriminate between models with and without a subsurface ocean, whose existence has been recently questioned. This experiment would be the first high‐precision geodetic experiment from a landed asset on an icy moon, and would provide dramatic improvements in our knowledge of Titan's interior.

authors: Joakim Kjellsson;Wonsun Park
title: Millennial‐Scale Climate States Alter Atlantic Multidecadal Variability Mechanisms in a Climate Model
abstract: The Atlantic Multidecadal Variability (AMV) influences North Atlantic sea surface temperatures and regional climate phenomena such as European droughts and hurricane activity. Its mechanisms remain complex due to long timescales and ocean‐atmosphere interactions. Here, we analyze a 2000‐year pre‐industrial climate model simulation revealing that millennial‐scale variability modulates AMV characteristics. During warm phases, the AMV is driven by a strong Atlantic meridional overturning circulation (AMOC) and subsurface warming, indicating ocean circulation dominance. In cold phases, the AMV arises from atmospheric heat fluxes with surface‐confined warming and AMOC lagging AMV. These results demonstrate that millennial‐scale ocean variability influences AMV mechanisms and the AMV‐AMOC relationship, providing insights into North Atlantic climate variability and its potential predictability.

authors: Haiqin Chen;Kun Zhao;Xinyu Zhang;Hao Huang;Ang Zhou;Lijian Zhu
title: Combined Assimilation of Radar and AWS Data From Mesoscale Networks for the Record‐Breaking Heavy Rainfall in China
abstract: Radar data assimilation (DA) alone remains insufficient for precipitation forecasts due to the lack of thermodynamic information in the pre‐storm environment. This study investigates the assimilation of dense automatic weather station (AWS) observations from China's mesoscale network alongside radar during an extreme rainfall event caused by the remnant vortex of typhoon Haikui. Optimal sequence and scale representation of dense AWS observations within the operational two‐step DA framework are examined. Results demonstrate that adding regional AWS data to radar and national‐level observations significantly refines surface wind, temperature, and humidity analyses, directly enhancing precipitation forecasts. Notably, assimilating synoptic‐scale information followed by radar outperforms the reverse approach, as initial large‐scale increments stabilize subsequent convective‐scale updates, including stronger maritime airflow, enhanced low‐level convergence and atmospheric instability. Furthermore, despite ∼10 km spacing, AWS data function optimally as synoptic‐scale observations rather than convective‐scale, as the single‐layer temperature and humidity increments with very small decorrelation scales have limited impact in NWP models.

explanation: 该论文研究了气候变化对晴空湍流的影响，晴空湍流是大气环境中的一个重要参数，与航空安全密切相关。论文使用了多个气候模型来分析湍流强度指标的变化，这与大气环境遥感技术中的大气成分分析和空气质量监测有直接关系，因此该论文与大气环境遥感技术密切相关。
authors: Joana de Medeiros;Paul D. Williams
title: Global Multi‐Model Eddy Dissipation Rate Probability Density Functions for Clear‐Air Turbulence Under Climate Change
abstract: Atmospheric turbulence poses a major risk to aviation, and it is expected to intensify as a response to climate change. The probability density functions (PDFs) of dozens of different clear‐air turbulence (CAT) diagnostics have been found to shift to higher values in response to climate change, consistent with strengthened vertical wind shear at cruising altitudes. The response of the PDF of the eddy dissipation rate (EDR), which is the internationally endorsed measure of turbulence strength, has not previously been studied, however. This study aims to quantify the impacts of these changes in the upper–tropospheric and lower–stratospheric dynamics on global CAT by 2100. By converting 21 CAT diagnostics from multiple climate model simulations into EDR for the historical period of 1950–1980 and the future period of 2070–2100, we find greater probabilities in the right–hand tail of the PDF in the future period compared with the historical period. Multi‐diagnostic‐model metrics show relative increases of 1%–15% in light, 2%–20% in light‐to‐moderate, 3%–20% in moderate, 8%–45% in moderate‐to‐severe, and 10%–50% in severe CAT by the future period depending on scenarios, regions, and seasons. These findings indicate that CAT will become significantly more frequent across all aviation‐relevant intensity levels as the climate continues to change.

authors: Xiaokang Wang;Ming Xue;Yongjie Huang;Cuihong Wu;Xiaofang Wang;Jingyu Wang
title: Characteristics, Mechanisms, and Rainfall Impacts of Warm‐Season Boundary‐Layer Jets in the Dongting‐Poyang Lake Region, South of the Middle Reach of the Yangtze River, China
abstract: Boundary‐layer (BL) jets (BLJs) exhibit significant diurnal variations and can strongly influence precipitation. The Dongting‐Poyang Lake region of China experiences frequent BLJs and heavy rainfall, yet systematic studies remain limited. This study investigates southerly and northeasterly BLJs (SBLJs and NEBLJs) in the region, focusing on their spatiotemporal distributions, formation, and precipitation impacts. SBLJs occur most frequently in summer, characterized by strong, deep south–southwesterly flows with warm advection. SBLJs peak around 02:00 Beijing Time (BJT) and weaken after sunrise as the mixed BL develops, with a typical duration of 1–9 hr. NEBLJs occur mainly in spring and fall, featuring strong but shallow northeasterly flows. NEBLJs peak around 22:00 BJT, show weaker diurnal variability, with a higher proportion of long‐duration cases persisting into daytime. Daily‐mean BLJ winds depend on synoptic patterns, while nocturnal intensification is dominated by BL inertial oscillations. Daytime mixing weakens BL winds, and reduced nighttime friction enables inertial oscillations to strengthen BL flows. Differences in seasons, thermodynamic conditions, and BL depth modulate inertial oscillation phases. This causes NEBLJs to peak ∼4 hr earlier than SBLJs. SBLJ‐associated precipitation concentrates at the jet exit region and peaks during pre‐dawn to early morning. Nocturnal BLJ strengthening enhances moisture flux and convergence to favor rainfall, while daytime deviation winds suppress precipitation. NEBLJ precipitation occurs at the jet exit during pre‐dawn to early morning and on its left side in early evening. Of these, exit‐region rainfall results from moisture transport by BL northerly and overlying southerly, combined with terrain‐induced lift.

authors: Xiaodong Xie;Yang Xiang;Jianlin Hu
title: Responses of the Atmospheric Age of PM2.5 to Changes in Meteorology and Emissions in China From 2013 to 2020
abstract: The clean air actions in China since 2013 have decreased fine particulate matter (PM2.5) concentrations significantly, however, their impacts on the atmospheric age of PM2.5 remain unclear. Here, we updated the age‐resolved Community Multiscale Air Quality (CMAQ) model to quantify the impacts of changes in anthropogenic emissions and meteorological conditions on the atmospheric age of PM2.5 in China from 2013 to 2020. The results indicated that PM2.5 concentrations decreased by 39.6% in central‐eastern China, primarily driven by anthropogenic emission reductions. The mean atmospheric age of PM2.5 in most of China increased in April and July and decreased in October. In January, the mean age of PM2.5 increased by ∼8.5 hr in the Beijing‐Tianjin‐Hebei region, while it decreased by 5.8–6.7 hr in the Pearl River Delta. Meteorological conditions are the dominant factors influencing PM2.5 age, accounting for 56% in Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei, 39% in the Yangtze River Delta, 56% in the Pearl River Delta, 74% in the Sichuan Basin, and 60% in the Fenwei Plain. Emission reductions increased the atmospheric age of PM2.5 in most of China from 2013 to 2020, with a maximum increase of ∼16 hr during July and April. Our results demonstrate that the best time to start emission control under stable weather conditions needs to be 5–15 hr earlier than that on normal days. With the air quality continuously improving, future short‐term emission controls, especially for large public events, shall be started earlier than before.

authors: Guangqi Zhu;Zhexuan Xu;Xu Wang;Ruhua Zhang;Wen Zhou
title: Modulation of the Stratospheric Polar Vortex on the Precipitation Dipole Mode in Southeast China During Early‐to‐Mid Winter
abstract: In this study, we investigated the linkage between the stratospheric polar vortex (SPV) and precipitation in early and mid winter (November–January; NDJ) in Southeast China, using station observations and reanalysis data sets, and verified the linkage using numerical stratospheric nudging model experiments. The results reveal that the SPV has a weak influence on the first empirical orthogonal function (EOF1) mode of precipitation over Southeast China on the interannual timescale, while the second mode (EOF2) characterized by a dipole pattern is related to the strength of SPV with a max 0.49 correlation coefficient. The downward‐propagating SPV signal modulates a Eurasian Rossby wave train characterized by anomalous cyclonic circulation over the Ural sector and anomalous anticyclonic circulation centered near Lake Baikal, corresponding to a weakened Ural ridge and an enhanced Lake Baikal ridge. This circulation configuration alters cold‐air intrusion and contributes to the meridional precipitation dipole over southeastern China. The moisture budget diagnosis shows that this geopotential height anomaly influences the dipole pattern mainly through the vertical dynamic component. Horizontal dynamic and thermodynamic components both exhibit a monopole over southeastern China, however, their effects are opposite. Nudging experiments based on the historical SPV are conducted to disentangle the contribution of the SPV. The stratospheric nudging experiment reproduces parts of the observed circulation and precipitation‐dipole structure. Projection onto the observed EOF2 pattern shows that the ensemble‐reproducible signal accounts for approximately 10% of the simulated PC2 variance, indicating that SPV variability provides a detectable but limited contribution, while atmospheric internal variability remains dominant.

authors: Ting Wu;Daohong Wang;Qingliu Yang;Robert Holzworth;David M. Smith;Yuuki Wada;Kazuhiro Nakazawa;Masashi Kamogawa;Tomoyuki Suzuki
title: A Survey of Energetic Compact Strokes in Japan
abstract: Energetic compact strokes (ECSs) are a special type of cloud‐to‐ground (CG) lightning stroke that were found to be consistently associated with downward terrestrial gamma‐ray flashes (TGFs). In this paper, we made a survey of ECSs in a 500‐km‐radius region in Japan using three years of data from the Fast Antenna Lightning Mapping Array (FALMA), a low‐frequency lightning location system. We found that the vast majority of ECSs occur in winter thunderstorms, especially in November and December, along the west coast of Japan. Compared with normal CG strokes, ECSs in winter are more likely to cluster in mountain regions with elevations of a few hundred meters. The tendency of ECSs to cluster in certain regions provides clear guidance for future campaigns to look for downward TGFs, but it also implies the increased possibility of health hazards posed by downward TGFs in these regions. Some ECSs also occur in spring and mostly at high mountain tops. ECSs have a clear tendency to be temporally isolated from other lightning discharges and rarely occur in thunderstorms with high flash rates. Based on these characteristics, we discuss the favorable conditions for the production of ECSs. A comparison with superbolts observed by the World Wide Lightning Location Network (WWLLN) shows that out of 10 superbolts observed near Japan, nine are negative CG strokes having similar FALMA waveforms as ECSs. It is possible that a significant fraction of WWLLN superbolts are also ECSs, and we suggest that ECSs can also be commonly found outside of Japan.

title: Quantifying Natural Hydrogen‐Helium Sources and Dynamic Accumulation in Global Sedimentary Basins
abstract: Despite the scientific and economic importance of hydrogen and helium, their crustal budgets remain poorly quantified. This study systematically assesses the accumulation of natural hydrogen and helium in global sedimentary basins by integrating predictive models for both gases with H2/He ratios. The predictive model infers natural hydrogen resources in global sedimentary basins of 100–106 Mt (megatons), with a most probable estimate of 1.7 × 103 Mt, and subsurface helium resources of 17.9 Mt. Water–rock reactions and the decay of radioactive elements within crystalline basement rocks generate natural hydrogen and helium, respectively, supplying background gas fluxes to overlying sedimentary basins. Mantle degassing and source rocks within sedimentary sequences provide supplementary gas contributions, resulting in an underestimation of these resources. This study reveals that global sedimentary basins host significant accumulations of natural hydrogen and helium resources—a finding that warrants increased attention.

authors: A. Cisneros‐Pineda;I. Haqiqi;J. Liu;S. Zuidema;D. Grogan
title: Quantifying the Impacts of Excess Water on Agricultural Losses and the Role of Adaptive Infrastructure
abstract: Excess water during the planting season is a growing source of production and income risk for agriculture. Yet its impacts remain poorly quantified. Existing studies typically rely on precipitation‐based indicators and therefore miss how soil saturation, runoff dynamics, and adaptive infrastructure shape crop failure. This paper fills that gap by integrating high‐resolution hydrologic model outputs with county‐level reports of failed and prevented planting across the U.S. Midwest from 2009 to 2020. We construct process‐based measures of runoff and soil moisture and evaluate their ability to explain losses while explicitly accounting for the presence of subsurface drainage systems. Hydrologic indicators strongly predict planting‐season losses: one additional day above the 95th‐percentile runoff threshold was associated with increase in failed or prevented acres by 0.37–0.42 percent. Counties with extensive artificial drainage see up to a 4.38 percent reduction in failed acres (up to 87% reduction in planting risk). Aggregated across the region, subsurface drainage preserved an estimated $13.53 billion in avoided agricultural losses over the study period. The results demonstrate that model‐derived excess‐water metrics outperform precipitation in most model setups. In particular, runoff‐based measures become especially informative when accounting for interactions with subsurface drainage infrastructure, highlighting how hydrologic context shapes crop susceptibility to excess water. The findings show the value of integrating hydrologic processes and adaptive infrastructure into agricultural risk assessment within coupled human–environment systems. Despite the value of drainage demonstrated here, future integrative work must consider potential tradeoffs imposed by nitrate concentrations and export.

title: De novo design of enantioselective artificial metalloenzyme photocatalysts
abstract: De novo design of enantioselective artificial metalloenzyme photocatalysts The ability to create protein scaffolds that impart enantioselectivity to simple, readily available metal catalysts could redefine the landscape of asymmetric catalysis. Artificial metalloenzymes (ArMs), hybrid catalysts that combine a synthetic metal cofactor with a protein scaffold, offer a potential means to achieve this goal, but scaffold discovery has remained constrained by trial-and-error approaches and the functional limits of extant proteins.1–5 This challenge is acute for metal polypyridine photocatalysts, which are widely used in visible-light chemistry but have not enabled highly enantioselective photocatalysis within protein scaffolds. In this study, we show that generative protein design6–8 can create de novo scaffolds that selectively bind these photocatalysts and that directed evolution converts the resulting artificial metalloenzymes into efficient, highly enantioselective photocatalysts9. The evolved proteins support diverse light-driven reactions, high catalyst turnover and catalyst recycling, and can function with commercially available racemic metal complexes. Spectroscopic studies show that the protein environment extends the photocatalyst excited-state lifetime and organizes substrate near the cofactor, altering energy transfer and controlling stereoselectivity. These findings establish de novo protein design as a route to functional scaffolds for synthetic metal complexes that lack natural protein partners and provide a strategy for combining protein design and evolution to control non-natural catalytic chemistry.

abstract:
Now that hyperacute rejection of pig xenografts can be reliably prevented, subtler immune-mediated graft injuries have emerged that conventional diagnostics often miss; a multimodal precision diagnostic framework is proposed to detect these injuries earlier, guide personalized immunosuppression and inform future gene editing strategies. 
 Recent breakthroughs in pig-to-human xenotransplantation have successfully prevented hyperacute rejection of kidney, heart, liver and lung xenografts, marking a milestone long considered a critical barrier. However, these major advances also brought new challenges into focus, as immune-mediated graft injuries including antibody-mediated rejection, T cell-mediated rejection and innate immune activation have been observed in most xenotransplantation procedures to date. Detection and management of these injuries remain a critical bottleneck, as conventional histopathology and standard clinical monitoring lack the sensitivity required to identify subclinical injury early enough to guide timely intervention. This diagnostic gap underscores an urgent need for the development of advanced, multimodal precision diagnostic frameworks to enhance immune surveillance, which will be essential for standardizing clinical protocols and enabling pathogenesis-driven therapeutic intervention. This approach will inform both immunosuppressive regimens and future gene editing strategies aimed at engineering rejection-resistant porcine organs, ultimately prolonging graft survival. Broad adoption of such an integrative strategy will be essential to transition xenotransplantation from an experimental intervention into a safe, scalable and patient-centred clinical therapy. In this Review, we synthesize recent progress in xenotransplantation and position multimodal precision diagnostics as a pivotal strategy to address the remaining immunological and clinical barriers to widespread clinical implementation. Now that hyperacute rejection of pig xenografts can be reliably prevented, subtler immune-mediated graft injuries have emerged that conventional diagnostics often miss; a multimodal precision diagnostic framework is proposed to detect these injuries earlier, guide personalized immunosuppression and inform future gene editing strategies.

abstract:
Salt marsh platforms resist erosion under extreme waves, but vegetation damage reduces wave attenuation; substantial wave attenuation by vegetation is mainly limited to low-energy marsh coasts with waves below 1 m. 
 Salt marshes protect coastlines by attenuating wind waves with their elevated marsh platform and above-ground vegetation1. Confidence in the persistence of this service under a changing climate requires knowledge on how extreme storms damage the platform and vegetation; however, a comprehensive, quantified understanding of salt marsh–wave interactions under extreme events is lacking. A unique experiment was conducted by transferring intact salt marsh to one of the world’s largest wave flumes, and subsequently exposing it to increasingly higher waves that reach up to 2 m significant wave height. We show that marsh substrates can persist with negligible erosion, despite cumulative wave exposure. By contrast, the vegetation was progressively damaged during continued wave exposure, gradually reducing vegetation-related wave attenuation. Results emphasize that vegetation was most effective in attenuating waves at low-energy marsh coasts (up to 1 m), where attenuation exceeded 10% (up to 50%), whereas attenuation at high-energy marsh coasts (wave height > 1 m) does not exceed 10%. Our global assessment supports the differentiation between low- and high-energetic conditions resulting from the flume experiment. Our results suggest that the marsh platform remains stable under extreme wave events and that substantial wave attenuation by marsh vegetation is limited to low-energy marsh coasts. title: Zeolite-catalysed olefin carbonylation based on tuning spatial confinement
abstract:
The use of zeolites with an appropriate pore structure combined with a high CO/olefin ratio is shown to catalyse olefin carbonylation and produce primary and secondary carboxylic acids as the main products. 
 Carbonylation is an important process used to produce aldehydes, carboxylic acids and esters1–5 that is usually catalysed by homogeneous metal complexes with ligands and iodide promoters6–12. Koch has reported that protons of mineral acids can also catalyse carbonylation13. Previous studies have demonstrated that Brønsted acidic zeolites can act as a heterogeneous, Koch-type catalyst for carbonylation of alcohols and olefins, but the products in this case are limited to tertiary carboxylic acids14–18. Here we show that targeted use of spatial confinement in a zeolite together with a high CO/olefin ratio can help break this limitation. We report that, with FER zeolite and a CO/olefin ratio of 360, olefin carbonylation can produce primary and secondary carboxylic acids as the main products; ethylene carbonylation to propanoic acid (PA) is achieved with 80% selectivity over 100 h and propylene carbonylation to isobutyric acid (IBA) is achieved with 95% selectivity over 750 h. The propylene and ethylene carbonylation selectivities decrease to 61% and 57%, respectively, as the CO/olefin ratio decreases to 24 and 90, respectively. Experiments in combination with theoretical calculations suggest that T2-O5 in eight-membered ring (8-MR) cavities of FER zeolite are the primary active sites for ethylene carbonylation and T3-O1 in ten-membered rings (10-MRs) are the primary active sites for propylene carbonylation. Our findings open new directions for olefin carbonylation and provide critical insights into the prerequisites for developing new zeolite-based carbonylation processes. title: Cold activates a BH2 metabolic network promoting longevity and proteostasis
abstract:
A multi-tissue signalling system links cold temperature to enhanced longevity and proteostasis in Caenorhabditis elegans. 
 Moderately cold temperatures extend lifespan and promote health across species1–3, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying these benefits remain unclear. Here we define a metabolite-driven, multi-tissue signalling system that links cold temperature to enhanced longevity and proteostasis in Caenorhabditis elegans. Cold temperature upregulates the biopterin-synthesis enzyme CAT-4 (GCH1 in humans), increasing production of dihydrobiopterin (BH2), a transportable reservoir for the bioactive cofactor tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4). BH2 is produced in muscle and transported to distal tissues, including the intestine and neurons, where it is converted into BH4 by the salvage enzyme DHFR-1. BH4 functions as an essential cofactor for phenylalanine hydroxylase PAH-1, promoting tyrosine synthesis and extending lifespan. This BH2–BH4 axis also prevents disease-related protein aggregation and subsequent neuronal dysfunction during ageing. Importantly, increasing BH2 synthesis specifically in muscle is sufficient to promote longevity and suppress pathological protein aggregation in distal tissues, even at normal or elevated temperatures. In human cells, BH2 or tyrosine supplementation reduces aggregation of polyQ-expanded proteins associated with Huntington’s disease, as well as mutant variants of TDP-43 and FUS that cause amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. Together, these findings identify BH2 as a cold-induced metabolite of which the synthesis, intertissue transport and conversion into bioactive BH4 preserve organism-wide proteostasis and extend lifespan. title: WEE1 opposes APC/C<sup>CDH1</sup> activity to promote S phase entry
abstract:
Experimental and modelling data indicate that WEE1 promotes re-entry of quiescent cells into the cell cycle, potentially explaining the toxic side effects of WEE1 inhibitors in cancer therapies. 
 WEE1 phosphorylates and inhibits the activity of cyclin-dependent kinases to prevent mitotic entry and establish a G2 DNA damage checkpoint1–3. Consequently, WEE1 inhibitors have been developed to be synthetically lethal in TP53-mutated tumours that become reliant on this WEE1-mediated checkpoint, and such inhibitors are undergoing clinical trials. However, WEE1 inhibitors also have efficacy in TP53-wild-type tumours, and many trials have been terminated owing to high levels of toxic side effects, suggesting that WEE1 has unknown functions. Here we show that WEE1 promotes cell cycle re-entry from quiescence (G0) by opposing the activity of the E3 ubiquitin ligase, anaphase-promoting complex–cyclosome bound to CDH1 (APC/CCDH1). WEE1 phosphorylates CDH1 (FZR1) at key residues that mediate the interaction between CDH1 and APC/C. Cells with loss of function of WEE1 during G0/G1 have delayed S phase entry, impaired G1/S transition, abnormal S phase accumulation of cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor p21Cip1/Kip1 and a p21-dependent G2 arrest. Reduced expression of APC/CCDH1 or p21 renders cells more sensitive to acute WEE1 inhibition, and both pathways are downregulated in cells with acquired WEE1 inhibitor resistance. These results reveal a mechanism of cell cycle control that has implications for how WEE1 inhibitors should be used in the clinic. title: A single archaeon couples long-chain fatty acid oxidation to methanogenesis
abstract:
Methanoglobus dolicholipophagus AA-75 is a thermophilic archaeon isolated from a Chinese petroleum reservoir that converts methanol into methane, carbon dioxide and acetate, and uses saturated and unsaturated fatty acids to produce methane. 
 Anaerobic degradation of complex organic compounds to methane and carbon dioxide is common in the deep subsurface biosphere and has long been considered to require syntrophic cooperation, with methanogens confined to the terminal use of simple C1 and C2 substrates. Thermodynamic considerations, multi-omics analyses and microcosm experiments suggest that archaeal lineages are capable of methanogenic degradation of complex substrates1–6. However, experimental validation in pure culture was lacking. Here we report the isolation of a thermophilic archaeon, Methanoglobus dolicholipophagus AA-75, affiliated with Archaeoglobi, from a Chinese petroleum reservoir. Strain AA-75 not only converts methanol into methane, carbon dioxide and acetate, but also uses saturated fatty acids varying from C7:0 to C18:0 and unsaturated fatty acids including C16:1, C18:1 and C18:2 to produce methane. We term the latter lipotrophic methanogenesis, which integrates β-oxidation of fatty acids with the Wood–Ljungdahl pathway and the canonical methyl-tetrahydromethanopterin:coenzyme M methyltransferase and methyl-coenzyme M reductase complexes, together with an intracellular electron transfer system. A formaldehyde-methanol branch probably functions as an auxiliary route for C1 metabolism during methanogenesis. Methane produced from stearate is moderately 13C-enriched (δ13C–CH4 = −40.0‰ to −36.3‰), distinct from the strong 13C depletion characteristic of canonical methanogenic pathways. These findings demonstrate that methanogens can function as primary degraders of complex organic matter, challenging the classical syntrophic paradigm and calling for refinement of current models of carbon cycling in the deep subsurface biosphere. title: An environmentally regulated dichotomy in cell lineages of the root
abstract:
An environment-regulated state is identified across multiple cell types at the root tip, revealing a shared dichotomy between cells with and without this state. 
 Plant development is highly plastic, with growth and architecture continuously shaped by environmental conditions. Roots, for instance, adjust their development to local water, nutrient and soil conditions. Despite this plasticity, individual root cell types are generally viewed as largely homogeneous populations that progress along a single developmental trajectory1. Here we show that rather than progressing along a single developmental trajectory, most Arabidopsis root cell lineage trajectories exhibit a stereotyped bifid topology, as revealed by single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcript mapping. One branch is characterized by a transcriptional program that is shared across multiple cell types and enriched for genes associated with environmental responses, including abscisic acid (ABA) signalling. This state occurs reproducibly in a subset of cells across multiple cell types, independent of developmental lineage, thereby revealing an additional layer of root cell identity. It is conserved across Arabidopsis ecotypes and persists despite major perturbations in developmental identity. Moreover, it is reduced in ABA-deficient and ABA-insensitive mutants and becomes more prevalent under water-deficit conditions. Together, these findings reveal an additional layer of root cell identity that is superimposed on developmental lineage and its prevalence is modulated by environmental conditions. These results uncover a previously unrecognized source of environment-associated transcriptional heterogeneity shared across root cell types. An environment-regulated state is identified across multiple cell types at the root tip, revealing a shared dichotomy between cells with and without this state.

title: CD51 delineates functionally distinct astrocyte subtypes in neural circuits
abstract:
CD51+ astrocytes promote synapse formation in the developing cortex, circuit plasticity in the hippocampus and circuit remodelling after stroke. 
 Astrocytes perform a diverse range of tasks that facilitate brain physiology, raising the possibility that these diverse astrocytic roles are enabled by functionally distinct subtypes1,2. Recent studies identified molecular diversity among astrocytes3; however, whether this molecular heterogeneity reflects specialized astrocyte subpopulations with distinct functions remains unclear. Here, on the basis of previous molecular and functional studies4, we generated a CD51-FLP mouse line that enables direct comparison of the functional properties between CD51+ and CD51− astrocyte subpopulations in neural circuits in vivo. We show that CD51+ and CD51− astrocytes have unique morphological, physiological and developmental properties in both the cortex and hippocampus. Functional studies demonstrate that CD51+ astrocytes selectively promote synapse formation in the developing cortex and circuit plasticity in the hippocampus. Mechanistically, we found that CD51+ astrocytes function through glypican 6 to promote synapse formation in the cortex, while CD51 itself drives circuit plasticity in the hippocampus. Applying these findings to brain injury, we found that CD51+ astrocytes promote functional recovery after stroke through enhanced synaptic remodelling. Taken together, our studies identify specialized astrocyte subpopulations that exhibit distinct functional properties in the developing, mature and injured brain. title: Persistent neuronal stress signalling underlies Angelman syndrome phenotypes
abstract:
Genetic and proteomic analyses in human neurons and mouse models of Angelman syndrome (AS) show that loss of the ubiquitin ligase UBE3A leads to an overabundance of asparagine synthetase, and that this is linked with many AS phenotypes. 
 Angelman syndrome is a severe neurodevelopmental disorder caused by the loss of UBE3A, a gene that encodes an E3 ubiquitin ligase1,2. The mechanisms that underlie Angelman syndrome are not well understood, and in particular, the link between UBE3A substrates and disease phenotypes remains uncertain3. Here, using gain- and loss-of-function mutations in UBE3A4,5 along with unbiased proteomics, we show that asparagine synthetase (ASNS) is a target of UBE3A. We find that ASNS protein abundance is increased in the brains of Ube3a-null mice and in human neurons6. Genetic correction of ASNS overabundance rescues microcephaly and many behavioural deficits. Detailed molecular analyses show that ASNS overabundance activates stress signalling and causes a global reduction in neuronal protein synthesis. Our results suggest that loss of UBE3A traps neurons in a state of persistent stress and stunts neuronal growth during developmentally sensitive periods. Moreover, our results indicate that targeting ASNS and the stress response could hold therapeutic potential in Angelman syndrome. title: Structural basis for protocadherin-1 recognition by New World hantaviruses
abstract:
The structure of PCDH1 bound to the ANDV spike defines the structural determinants of hantavirus–receptor recognition. 
 Hantaviruses are rodent-borne pathogens that cause severe human disease for which no approved therapeutics are available. New World hantaviruses, including Andes virus (ANDV), use the cell-surface receptor protocadherin-1 (PCDH1) to enter host cells1. However, the structural basis of this interaction remains unclear. Here we describe the structure of PCDH1 bound to the ANDV spike at near-atomic resolution. PCDH1 asymmetrically engages a deep central pocket formed by four Gn protomers in the spike, explaining why only intact viral particles or soluble tetramers recognize it. Mutagenesis identified three Gn loops that shape the receptor-binding site and afford the transfer of PCDH1 binding from New World to Old World glycoproteins. Structural and functional analyses of four neutralizing antibodies revealed that they block receptor binding through two distinct mechanisms—occluding access to the PCDH1-binding site or sterically preventing receptor engagement. Together, these findings define the structural determinants of hantavirus–receptor recognition, reveal how a virus can mask its receptor-binding site by recessing it in a surface depression and how antibodies can counter this strategy, and provide a framework for the design of antiviral therapeutics targeting the hantavirus spike. The structure of PCDH1 bound to the ANDV spike defines the structural determinants of hantavirus–receptor recognition.

title: GRP75-dependent SIMPA mediates inter-organellar quality control
abstract:
Proteotoxic stress drives formation of GRP75-dependent protein aggregates that signal through mitochondria–ER contact sites to activate targeted quality-control pathways, enabling selective clearance of damaged proteins and preserving mitochondrial integrity. 
 Mitochondria are bound by a double membrane and are semiautonomous organelles, rendering them highly vulnerable to global and internal proteostatic stress1. Multiple surveillance mechanisms at proteostatic and inter-organellar levels have evolved to maintain mitochondrial integrity and cellular health2–7. However, the precise mechanisms by which proteostatic damage relays stress signals across organelles and how the quality surveillance machinery coordinates these functions remain unknown. Here we report that under proteostatic stress, damaged mitochondrial proteins are sequestered to form stress-induced mitochondrial protein aggregates (SIMPAs) that activate specific quality control mechanisms in a spatially confined manner without perturbing the mitochondrial network. Quantitative proteomic and correlative light–electron microscopy analysis revealed that SIMPA mediates inter-organellar communication via mitochondria–endoplasmic reticulum contact sites or mitochondrial-associated membranes. Mechanistically, GRP75 coordinates SIMPA biogenesis and focally activates endoplasmic reticulum unfolded protein response pathways via mitochondria–endoplasmic reticulum contact sites or mitochondrial-associated membranes for the targeted clearance of SIMPAs. Functionally, in both cellular and liver disease models, we found that a GRP75-dependent SIMPA signalling cascade attenuates mitochondrial stress and preserves mitochondrial integrity under proteotoxic stress. Overall, we show that SIMPAs, functioning as protein condensates, serve as a central cross-compartment communication hub for mitochondrial quality control, supporting cellular and organismal fitness. Proteotoxic stress drives formation of GRP75-dependent protein aggregates that signal through mitochondria–ER contact sites to activate targeted quality-control pathways, enabling selective clearance of damaged proteins and preserving mitochondrial integrity.

title: Programmable design of functional proteins from natural language
abstract:
Pinal, a 16-billion-parameter artificial intelligence model, designs functional proteins from natural-language descriptions, demonstrating experimentally validated activities and improved CO2-fixation product yields without iterative optimization. 
 Programming biological function—designing bespoke proteins to perform specified molecular tasks—is a foundational goal of molecular engineering. However, current design models remain fundamentally limited1–3: they typically require either natural proteins as starting points for optimization or manual reformulation of functional goals as geometric and sequence-level constraints to guide candidate generation. Here we introduce Pinal, a 16-billion-parameter foundation model that designs candidate proteins from natural-language descriptions of desired function. Trained on 1.7 billion synthetically annotated protein–text pairs, Pinal links functional intent to protein sequence and structure. In computational evaluations, generated candidates combined high predicted foldability with functional-description alignment and sequence diversity, providing a basis for prioritizing experimentally testable designs. We applied Pinal to four distinct design tasks—a fluorescent protein, a polyethylene terephthalate hydrolase, an alcohol dehydrogenase and a metabolic H-protein—and experimentally observed the intended function in each case, including catalytic activity for both designed enzymes. Without iterative experimental optimization, a Pinal-designed H-protein increased product titre by 1.7-fold relative to the corresponding native Escherichia coli H-protein in a multi-enzyme CO2 fixation pathway. These findings support natural language as a high-level interface for candidate generation in protein design, enabling programmable exploration with reduced reliance on manually specified structural or sequence constraints. Pinal, a 16-billion-parameter artificial intelligence model, designs functional proteins from natural-language descriptions, demonstrating experimentally validated activities and improved CO2-fixation product yields without iterative optimization.

title: Octupole-driven spin torque switching of antiferromagnetic tunnel junctions
abstract:
All-antiferromagnetic tunnel junctions can display both a large TMR and a reciprocal switching effect, octupole-driven spin-transfer torque, enabling nanoscale magnetic memory and potentially room-temperature terahertz spintronic devices. 
 Magnetic tunnel junctions based on ferromagnets are canonical devices in spintronics, with wide-ranging applications in data storage, computing and sensing. They simultaneously exhibit mechanisms for electrical detection and control of magnetic order through the tunnelling magnetoresistance (TMR)1–5 and spin-transfer torque6–9 effects, respectively. It was long assumed that neither of these effects could be sizeable in all-antiferromagnetic tunnel junctions (AATJs), considering that they have no net magnetization. However, it was recently shown that AATJs based on chiral antiferromagnets do exhibit TMR due to their non-relativistic momentum-dependent spin polarization and cluster magnetic octupole moment, which are manifestations of their spin–split band structure10–13. However, the reciprocal effect, that is, the antiferromagnetic counterpart of spin–transfer torque, has been assumed non-existent due to the total electric current being spin-neutral. Here we report nanoscale AATJs that display this reciprocal effect, which we term octupole-driven spin-transfer torque (OTT). We demonstrate current-induced OTT switching of PtMn3|MgO|PtMn3 AATJs, with a TMR value of 363% at room temperature and switching current densities of the order of 10 MA cm–2. Our theoretical modelling explains the origin of OTT in terms of the imbalance between intra- and inter-sublattice spin currents across the AATJ, and, equivalently, in terms of the non-zero net cluster octupole polarization of each PtMn3 layer. This work establishes a new materials platform for antiferromagnetic spintronics and provides a pathway towards deeply scaled magnetic memory and room-temperature terahertz technologies. All-antiferromagnetic tunnel junctions can display both a large TMR and a reciprocal switching effect, octupole-driven spin-transfer torque, enabling nanoscale magnetic memory and potentially room-temperature terahertz spintronic devices.

title: Amazon carbon emissions driven by human actions amplified by droughts
abstract:
Fifteen years of atmospheric CO2 measurements show that the Amazon carbon sink is weakening, with fires, deforestation and climate stress driving increasingly high carbon emissions. 
 The Amazon carbon sink is weakening as deforestation1–5, rising tree mortality6–8 and climate change disrupt the climatic conditions that sustain a humid tropical forest9–11. Forest loss reduces precipitation, increases temperatures and lengthens the dry season, driving higher carbon emissions1–4,11,12. Climate stress is stronger in more deforested regions, rendering forests progressively more flammable1,9,13. Large-scale climate events, such as El Niño, further amplify regional climate impacts9,14–17. Here we present an analysis of 15 years of Amazonian carbon fluxes derived from atmospheric CO2 measurements. We determine a carbon balance of 0.32 ± 0.08 PgC yr−1, with fires acting as the dominant source (0.40 ± 0.07 PgC yr−1) and forest uptake becoming increasingly unable to offset emissions. Furthermore, we investigate key drivers of the carbon emissions of Amazonia and identify three distinct year groups. Group 1 (2011–2014, 2017 and 2018) represents the role of the Amazon in the global carbon balance (0.11 ± 0.08 PgC yr−1) during wetter years with low human activity, such as deforestation, biomass burning and degradation. Group 2 (2019–2022) represents Amazon carbon emissions (0.43 ± 0.13 PgC yr−1) from human activities (mainly deforestation and degradation) during years with low climatic stress. Group 3 (2010, 2015, 2016, 2023 and 2024) has the highest carbon emissions (0.49 ± 0.07 PgC yr−1) and comprises warm and dry years (high climate stress), such as El Niño and the warming of the Tropical North Atlantic Ocean, associated with biomass burning. Fifteen years of atmospheric CO2 measurements show that the Amazon carbon sink is weakening, with fires, deforestation and climate stress driving increasingly high carbon emissions.

title: The proteome of Middle Pleistocene Xujiayao and common Denisovan morphology
abstract:
Denisovans from the Xujiayao and other East Asian sites are morphologically distinctive, with a low cranial profile with near-parallel lateral walls, a massive supraorbital torus, a flat zygomaxillary region and weak prognathism. 
 The taxonomy and phylogeny of late Middle Pleistocene hominins in East Asia remain highly debated1. Xujiayao, a key representative assemblage with many fossils and a clear stratigraphy dating to around 199–138 thousand years ago, has been extensively studied, but its evolutionary position remains uncertain. Here, to clarify this, we analysed Xujiayao material through both palaeoproteomic analysis and morphological comparisons with other East Asian late Middle Pleistocene archaic Homo. Proteomic analysis of two specimens identified 18 endogenous proteins, and the Denisova-specific COL1A2-996 R>K mutation strongly supported their affiliation with the Denisovan lineage. Extended analysis identifies a set of shared morphological traits between Denisovan fossils (Xujiayao and Harbin) and other East Asian late Middle Pleistocene archaic Homo (such as Jinniushan, Dali and Hualongdong), indicating that they all belong to the Denisovan lineage. This analysis provides a comprehensive view of Denisovan features, showing both traits reminiscent of Homo erectus (such as a thick cranial vault) and those characteristic of modern humans (for example, a strongly arched temporal squama). They also share features with late Neanderthals, such as the structure of the temporal labyrinth and the presence of a suprainiac fossa. Notably, Denisovans are distinctive, with a low cranial profile with near-parallel lateral walls, a massive supraorbital torus, a flat zygomaxillary region and weak prognathism.
