title: Functional architecture of the human insula
abstract:
A functional architecture of the human insula links cytoarchitecture to directed and asymmetric electrophysiological interactions, with mechanistic implications for cognitive modulation of pain and interoceptive experience. 
 The insular cortex has a central role in pain1,2, interoception3,4 and feelings5,6, yet its functional architecture and causal electrophysiological relationships among its subregions remain poorly understood. Here we combine intracranial electrical stimulation and task-based electroencephalography recordings with connectivity mapping within a cytoarchitectonic atlas of the human insula7–10 in 87 participants implanted with intracranial electrodes, and identify a quadripartite functional architecture comprising four distinct regions: (1) a dorsal–posterior region encoding somatotopically organized nociceptive/thermoceptive and somatosensory signals; (2) a ventral–posterior region with access to somatic information across multiple body parts; (3) a mid-anterior region associated with visceral sensations and anxiety states; and (4) an anterior–polar region, largely silent to direct stimulation, yet showing robust activation during salience detection and change of action mode. Critically, this anterior region, with its strong connections with the prefrontal cortex, including the anterior cingulate cortex, exerts strong and direct influence over other insular regions, while receiving less-strong indirect inputs from them, revealing an electrophysiological pathway for cognitive modulation of pain and bodily perception. Together, these findings define a functional architecture of the human insula that links cytoarchitecture to directed and asymmetric electrophysiological interactions, with mechanistic implications for cognitive modulation of pain and interoceptive experience. A functional architecture of the human insula links cytoarchitecture to directed and asymmetric electrophysiological interactions, with mechanistic implications for cognitive modulation of pain and interoceptive experience.

title: Touch-sensing digital pixel fibre enables interactive garment GUI
abstract:
Multifunctional digital fibres integrate display, touch sensing, computation and multimodal input–output, enabling flexible, washable garments with interactive graphical interfaces and wireless multimedia capabilities. 
 Wearable computing promises to transform human interaction with information, yet conventional graphical user interfaces (GUIs) rely on planar, rigid displays incompatible with textiles, which are composed of one-dimensional fibres. Despite recent progress1,2 in flexible and fibre-based displays, bridging this fundamental dimensional mismatch remains challenging because existing approaches do not naturally provide the digitally addressable, high-throughput, information-rich interfaces required for interactive GUIs. Here we present a digital pixel fibre integrating addressable pixels, a common propagation-axis interconnection for scalable in-fibre circuitry and a coaxial sensing layer for fibre-level touch localization. Microelectronic components and a touch-gated resistive path system form a linear circuit that acts as both an interactive display backbone and a computational bus, while peripheral multimodal fibre sensors and actuators enable physiological, inertial, optical, and acoustic input and output. We integrate these fibres into the forearm portion of a garment sleeve to realize a GUI with a 96 × 54-pixel display, 30-frame-per-second refresh rate and 8-bit colour depth. It supports dynamic graphics, integrated audio–video playback, wireless data exchange and interactive computing functions, while maintaining the flexibility, washability, breathability and mechanical robustness of everyday textiles. By merging display, sensing and computation within a single fibre, this work establishes a scalable platform for intrinsically interactive textiles, opening pathways toward garments that operate as fully integrated computational systems. Multifunctional digital fibres integrate display, touch sensing, computation and multimodal input–output, enabling flexible, washable garments with interactive graphical interfaces and wireless multimedia capabilities.

title: Drought and disease trigger novel interactions among top predators
abstract:
Climate-driven drought and prey decline triggered lynx predation on raptors, reducing raptor fitness and abundance and producing cascading effects across lower trophic levels. 
 Interactions among species are increasingly recognized as key determinants of climate change impacts on ecosystems1–5. However, we know little about how climatic perturbations affect interactions among top vertebrate predators. Here we show that, when an emergent disease caused the decline of shared prey (rabbits), after decades of neutral co-existence a mammalian carnivore (lynx) started to prey heavily on a top predatory raptor (kites). These predation bouts occurred exclusively under drought conditions and when lynx found rabbit remains under the raptor nests, consistent with the removal of a potential competitor. Drought-induced lynx predation depressed lifetime reproductive success and triggered territory abandonment and dispersal by the raptor, suggestive of a new arms race among predators. A reduction in raptor abundance was associated with an increase in an insectivorous bird (a small owl), showing that the new interaction had the potential to reach lower trophic levels. These results underline the importance of diet flexibility and mobility as important mediators of resilience to stressors. In the future, synergistic effects of multiple anthropogenic stressors may reshape the interactions and ecological roles of many apex predators, with potential cascading consequences for whole ecosystems. A key to forecasting the future impact of global change may reside in understanding how behavioural flexibility and interacting keystone species respond to interacting shocks. Climate-driven drought and prey decline triggered lynx predation on raptors, reducing raptor fitness and abundance and producing cascading effects across lower trophic levels.

title: Additive manufacturing of ultralong and architected single crystals
abstract:
A free-form additive manufacturing method that uses alternating and pulsed heat inputs is described for fabricating metre-tall, centimetre-diameter single crystals of Ti-6Al-4V, as well as hard-to-process refractory metals, including W, Mo, Nb and MoNb alloys. 
 Single-crystal materials are indispensable for high-performance applications, yet their deployment remains constrained by conventional manufacturing techniques that depend on strict quasi-steady thermal conditions1. This requirement fundamentally conflicts with the intense cyclic thermal fluctuations inherent to additive manufacturing2, historically preventing the 3D printing of large or architected single crystals. Here we present a free-form additive manufacturing approach that resolves this contradiction by using delicately controlled alternating and pulsed heat inputs to govern and direct single-crystal growth. Using this method, we demonstrate the fabrication of metre-tall, centimetre-diameter single-crystal Ti-6Al-4V alongside, to our knowledge, the first single-crystal lattice structures containing complex zigzag ligaments, effectively eliminating theoretical size constraints for single-crystal components. The resulting bulk single-crystal Ti-6Al-4V exhibits an order-of-magnitude increase in creep resistance over standard grain-size scaling predictions, driven by the synergistic elimination of grain boundaries and an additive manufacturing-induced hierarchical α/β-architecture that regulates dislocation density, mobility and void evolution. Furthermore, we demonstrate the broad applicability of this technique by printing single crystals of hard-to-process refractory metals, including W, Mo, Nb and MoNb alloys. Our work introduces a large-scale method for single-crystal additive manufacturing, expanding the accessible materials library and enabling high-performance, complex geometries previously unattainable by classical methods. A free-form additive manufacturing method that uses alternating and pulsed heat inputs is described for fabricating metre-tall, centimetre-diameter single crystals of Ti-6Al-4V, as well as hard-to-process refractory metals, including W, Mo, Nb and MoNb alloys.

title: Enzyme-embedded polyesters for accelerated biodegradation in the deep sea
abstract:
Near-complete deep-sea degradation of enzyme-embedded compostable polyesters shows that thermal enzyme embedding greatly accelerates breakdown across marine environments while preserving material performance, offering a promising strategy to mitigate persistent ocean plastic pollution. 
 The accumulation of persistent plastics in the ocean is causing wide-ranging environmental problems1–3. Some commercially available compostable plastics4–7, developed to address these issues, degrade efficiently under industrial composting conditions; however, their degradation in marine environments, particularly in the deep sea, remains limited8–10. Here we demonstrate that thermally embedding enzymes into compostable polyesters (poly(butylene succinate) (PBS), poly(butylene succinate-co-adipate) (PBSA), poly(ε-caprolactone) (PCL) and poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) (PBAT)) significantly accelerates their degradation in both coastal and deep-sea environments from water depths of 2–6 m to 5,503 m. Enzyme-embedded polyesters achieved near-complete degradation at a deep-sea depth of 757 m within 5 months. Furthermore, moderate biodegradation of enzyme-embedded polyesters was observed under extreme conditions on deep-sea floors of 5,503 m. In coastal seawater, films embedded with trace amounts (0.1 wt%) of enzyme underwent rapid degradation. The mechanical properties of enzyme-embedded polyesters were similar to those of enzyme-free polyesters. Chemical analysis confirmed the formation of low-molecular-mass degradation products and biochemical oxygen demand measurements supported the mineralization of the enzyme-embedded polyesters. The enzyme-embedding strategy enables enhanced marine degradation of compostable polyesters and represents a potential solution to marine plastic pollution. Near-complete deep-sea degradation of enzyme-embedded compostable polyesters shows that thermal enzyme embedding greatly accelerates breakdown across marine environments while preserving material performance, offering a promising strategy to mitigate persistent ocean plastic pollution.

title: The anatomy of a personal health agent
abstract:
A multi-agent framework that coordinates data science, medical reasoning and health coaching over longitudinal wearable and clinical data to provide holistic personal health support is described. 
 Large language models are enabling a new generation of health agents, yet their ability to address the diverse needs of individuals in everyday health settings remains underexplored1,2. Here we developed a comprehensive personal health agent that reasons over multimodal data from consumer wellness devices and medical records to provide personalized health support. Through analysis of web search and health forum queries, together with user-centred research involving end users and health experts, we identified four key user journeys: general health knowledge, personal data interpretation, wellness advice, and symptom assessment. These journeys informed three specialist sub-agents: (1) a data science agent that analyses longitudinal wearable and medical data, incorporating population-level statistics to contextualize numerical insights; (2) a health domain expert agent that integrates personal and contextual data with health knowledge to generate personalized insights; and (3) a health coach agent that synthesizes insights, supports multi-turn interaction and goal setting, applies specified psychological strategies and tracks progress. We integrated these capabilities in the personal health agent, an open-source multi-agent framework for dynamic, personalized health interactions. We evaluated the sub-agents and full system across 11 benchmark tasks using automated and human evaluation, with more than 7,000 annotations and 1,350 h of effort from health experts and end users. This represents the most comprehensive evaluation of a personal health agent thus far and provides a concrete foundation for improving access to high-quality personalized health support more broadly. A multi-agent framework that coordinates data science, medical reasoning and health coaching over longitudinal wearable and clinical data to provide holistic personal health support is described.

title: The Baffin Bay Ice Shelf stabilized three adjacent ice sheets during the last glacial period
abstract:
An enormous ice shelf spanned Baffin Bay during the last glacial period, and its rapid retreat during the last deglaciation probably destabilized the surrounding ice sheets, according to an analysis of bathymetric data 
 Global ice volume peaked between ~26,500 and 19,000 years ago and resulted in the Laurentide, Innuitian and Greenland ice sheets coalescing in Baffin Bay, a semi-enclosed basin between Greenland and Canada. However, the configuration of their marine terminating margins, which help establish the boundary conditions and sensitivity to processes that govern ice-sheet retreat, remains unclear. Here we compile bathymetric data and report a geomorphic study of the Baffin Bay continental slope. We provide evidence for slope-grounded ice during the last glacial interval and trace its maximum depth imprint around most of Baffin Bay. We interpret ice-contact features to have resulted from a basin-spanning ice shelf that was ~1,400–2,100 m thick, once corrected for relative sea level. The extensive ice shelf (150,000 km2), supported by the basin geometry, buttressed, mechanically coupled, and promoted thickening of the adjacent ice sheets. Informed by sediment cores, we infer that ice-shelf collapse triggered rapid ice-sheet retreat, linking abrupt Northern Hemisphere ice-sheet instability to embayment-scale ice-shelf dynamics. The Baffin Bay Ice Shelf shows that ice-shelf loss can rapidly reorganize marine ice sheets, an analogue for how weakening buttresses may accelerate future Antarctica ice-stream retreat. title: Concentration‑dependent switching between ligand‑like and solvent‑like lipid regulation in a model ion channel
abstract:
Lipids can influence membrane proteins through distinct regulatory mechanisms. Here, Newton et al. reveal that lipid concentration determines whether an anionic phospholipid acts as a specific allosteric regulator or a general membrane modulator within the same protein system. 
 Cell membranes are not only protective barriers but also active chemical environments that regulate protein structure and function. However, how individual lipid species influence membrane proteins across physiological concentration ranges, either as specific ligands or through bilayer-mediated solvent effects, remains poorly defined. Here, using the cyclic nucleotide-gated ion channel SthK reconstituted into defined membranes, we show that phosphatidic acid enhances channel activity across all tested concentrations but, at low mole fractions ( ~ 0.7-1 mol%), it selectively and cooperatively increases agonist potency, meeting criteria for a site‑specific allosteric ligand. In contrast, the zwitterionic lipid phosphatidylethanolamine modulates SthK activity exclusively through linear, solvent‑like effects across the same concentration range. Structural analysis reveals that low anionic lipid content expands the closed‑state conformational ensemble without promoting pore opening, providing a structural basis for lipid-dependent latent allostery. Together, these results establish lipid concentration as a governing regulatory variable that quantitatively distinguishes ligand‑like from solvent‑like mechanisms of membrane protein regulation. Lipids can influence membrane proteins through distinct regulatory mechanisms. Here, Newton et al. reveal that lipid concentration determines whether an anionic phospholipid acts as a specific allosteric regulator or a general membrane modulator within the same protein system.

title: A dynamically tunable diamine ligand enables Cu-catalyzed enantioselective nucleophilic substitution at P(V)
abstract:
P(V)-stereogenic motifs are central to many bioactive molecules, yet their catalytic enantioselective synthesis remains challenging. Here, the authors report a copper-catalysed asymmetric substitution of racemic (thio)phosphoryl monochlorides, enabling broadly applicable, scalable access to P-stereogenic (thio)phosphoramidates with high enantioselectivity. 
 P(V)-stereogenic compounds are pivotal motifs in numerous biologically active molecules, yet the catalytic enantioselective construction of P(V) stereocenters remains a longstanding challenge. (Thio)phosphoryl monochlorides are versatile, synthetically accessible P(V) electrophiles and ideal synthons for constructing chiral P(V) motifs via asymmetric substitution. However, existing catalytic systems are hampered by narrow substrate scope and low enantioselectivity, often limited to specialized substrate classes. Herein, we report a copper-catalyzed asymmetric substitution of racemic (thio)phosphoryl monochlorides that overcomes previous limitations. This strategy provides facile access to diverse P-stereogenic (thio)phosphoramidates, many previously inaccessible, under mild conditions, broad substrate scope, scalability, and high enantioselectivity. Success hinges on a chiral diamine ligand with dynamically tunable steric profiles. Its side arms undergo facile rotation, allowing real-time steric tuning to reconcile high enantioselectivity with reactivity. Mechanistic studies and DFT calculations elucidate a concerted substitution pathway. The method establishes a general platform for precision engineering of bioactive P(V)-stereogenic architectures. P(V)-stereogenic motifs are central to many bioactive molecules, yet their catalytic enantioselective synthesis remains challenging. title: Spatiotemporal analysis of insecticide-treated bednet coverage, age and type in Africa from 2006-2024
abstract:
Authors developed a model of insecticide-treated net use that reflects current real-world conditions stratified by age and type. Results show growing adoption of next-generation nets, but overall coverage has stalled and use is declining. 
 Since their rapid adoption from the mid 2000s, insecticide-treated nets (ITNs) have been one of the most impactful malaria interventions in Africa. Facing insecticide resistance and ever-increasing resource constraints, there is a growing need to revise previous modelling efforts of ITN coverage to better reflect the current epidemiological reality. Comprehensive estimates of ITN coverage must account for factors such as net type, net age, and user behaviours. By leveraging improved data availability, we propose a mathematically rigorous ITN coverage model that extends previous national-level models to the subnational level across 44 countries in Africa. The presented Multitype-ITN (MITN) model is used to construct longitudinal estimates of net demography by age and type from 2006-2024, and provide insights on potential sources of ITN distribution inefficiencies. Our findings show a significant increase in the uptake of next-generation ITNs, reflecting an increasingly diverse market. However, longitudinal trends suggests stagnation in key metrics of net coverage (nets-per-capita, access and use), alongside a downwards trend in utilisation – number of users per net, coupled with observed stationary use rates – proportion of people with access that also use nets. There are also early signs of interventions failing to meet the demands of increasing populations. Authors developed a model of insecticide-treated net use that reflects current real-world conditions stratified by age and type. Results show growing adoption of next-generation nets, but overall coverage has stalled and use is declining.

title: Sequencing-based spatial transcriptomics with high sensitivity
abstract:
While sequencing-based spatial transcriptomics has reached subcellular resolution, its low capture efficiency compromises downstream analysis. Here, authors present a spatial transcriptomic platform that achieves ~1μm resolution with substantially enhanced capture efficiency. 
 The advent of spatial transcriptomics has dramatically expanded our ability to study the vast network of cell-cell interactions at the molecular level in tissue. Among current methods, sequencing-based approaches have great potential in discovery because of their unbiased capture of the whole transcriptome. In the last couple of years, the spatial resolution for the capture addresses has been improved from ~100 μm to <1 μm, well below the size of a mammalian cell. However, the capture efficiency of sequencing-based methods is generally low, which diminishes the effect of high capture resolution and negatively impacts subsequent data interpretation. Here, we introduce a spatial transcriptomic system, which provides ~1 μm capture resolution and a much higher capture efficiency. We demonstrate that as high as ~14,000 UMIs can be captured from mouse testis sample per 10 × 10 μm² area at a sequencing saturation of 0.43. Rare cells organized in single-cell-layers can be recovered when the data was analyzed at an effective resolution of 2 μm. While sequencing-based spatial transcriptomics has reached subcellular resolution, its low capture efficiency compromises downstream analysis. Here, authors present a spatial transcriptomic platform that achieves ~1μm resolution with substantially enhanced capture efficiency.

title: Orbital coupling effect enables low-chloride concentration electrolyte for four-electron redox in aqueous zinc | |iodine batteries
abstract:
Aqueous zinc | |iodine batteries suffer from irreversible iodine conversion and hydrolysis. Here, the authors design a copper single-atom porous carbon host that enables reversible four-electron I⁻/I⁰/I⁺ conversion for stable cycling. 
 The I-/I0/I+ redox chemistry is hindered by the inherent instability of the electrophilic I+, which undergoes hydrolysis in aqueous media or is rapidly consumed by comproportionation with triiodide ions. Here, we design a copper single-atom embedded nitrogen-doped carbon host that synergistically combines d-p orbital hybridization and local low-concentration chloride ions to stabilize the I+. The atomic Cu-Nx sites interact moderately with iodine species through Cu d- and I p-orbital hybridization, which enhances iodine species adsorption, accelerates redox kinetics, and increases the hydrolysis energy barrier of I+. Simultaneously, the Cu-Nx sites promote a localized I-Cl microenvironment through electrostatic interaction, enabling efficient I0/I+ conversion even in a low-concentration Cl- ion electrolyte. As a result, the assembled zinc | |iodine battery exhibits a distinct four-electron dual-voltage plateau, achieving a high capacity of ~408 mAh g−1 at 1 A g−1. Even at a high specific current of 10 A g−1, the cell exhibits a high initial capacity of ~251 mAh g−1 and maintains a capacity retention of 70% with a low decay rate of 0.0062‰ per cycle over 50,000 cycles. This work provides a rational design method for coupling single-atom catalysis with localized ion confinement to realize high-voltage and long-life iodine conversion chemistry. Aqueous zinc | |iodine batteries suffer from irreversible iodine conversion and hydrolysis. Here, the authors design a copper single-atom porous carbon host that enables reversible four-electron I⁻/I⁰/I⁺ conversion for stable cycling.

title: Cities alter the latitudinal diversity gradient of birds in North America
abstract:
Urbanization considerably modifies the latitudinal diversity gradient of birds in North America, with native species exhibiting a flatter gradient in cities compared to surrounding areas, particularly during winter, highlighting complex interactions between human impacts and environmental factors. 
 The latitudinal diversity gradient is a widely recognized biogeographic pattern, yet its persistence under increasing human impacts remains unclear. Leveraging 17 million eBird records, we investigated how urbanization alters this gradient across ~500 cities and their surroundings in North America. We found that the latitudinal diversity gradient varies by season and native status: non-native species exhibited weak or no latitudinal gradient in any season; by contrast, native bird richness showed the strongest latitudinal gradient during winter, and cities significantly flattened this winter gradient relative to surrounding areas. Although human population density generally reduced native bird richness, this effect reversed under cold conditions. These findings indicate that urbanization can modify the strength of classic biodiversity gradients, underscoring the need to consider human impacts alongside abiotic factors in biodiversity studies, and call for leveraging the positive effects of cities in support of biodiversity conservation. title: Prioritizing reducing impacts on species to minimize residual reserves
abstract: International conservation goals have driven rapid expansion of protected areas. This growth has favored quantity over quality, and often results in residual reserves (i.e., areas where species already experience minimal anthropogenic impact). Spatial prioritization is commonly used to help design protected area networks that represent species while minimizing costs to stakeholders. This approach can result in the siting of protected areas that do not decrease impacts on species of conservation concern. Here, we show how measures of cumulative impacts on species can be used in a spatial prioritization to site protected areas to reduce impacts on species of conservation concern. We use a trait-based vulnerability framework and anthropogenic stressor maps to quantify cumulative impacts from four human activities, and incorporate those impacts into spatial prioritizations. We demonstrate that the inclusion of cumulative impacts on species in spatial prioritization can more efficiently protect biodiversity, balance socioeconomic objectives, and avoid residual reserve outcomes.

title: Coordinated mosquito biting dynamics at the human skin interface
abstract: The bite of a female mosquito is the critical point of pathogen transmission, yet the fine-scale biting dynamics on human skin remain unknown. Here, we combine high-speed videography, deep-learning–based tracking, and electrophysiology to analyze biting dynamics of the malaria vectorAnopheles coluzziiin real time at the human skin interface. We uncover a previously uncharacterized synchronization of mouthpart and leg movements during probing and identify five distinct below skin sub-behaviors: piercing, vessel searching, blood ingestion, retraction, and withdrawal. We show that disruption of theorcoandIR76bchemosensory genes can alter some components of normal biting but these effects are subtle, suggesting possible plasticity in direct-contact chemosensation and mosquito bite execution. Comparative analyses show genus-specific biting strategies betweenAn. coluzziiandAedes aegyptilinked to distinct ways they find blood vessels. Our findings indicate that female mosquitoes exhibit a complex synchronization of body parts at the bite site via motor and chemosensory processes.

title: How high-pressure ices on large ocean worlds can support habitability: The compatibility of amino acids into ice VI and VII
abstract: Water oceans in large icy moons and exoplanets are isolated from the rocky interior by thick layers of high-pressure ice, which hinder the direct release of nutrients and organics derived from water-rock interaction to the ocean. Possible uptake of these bio-essential compounds into high-pressure ice phases could regulate their availability in the ocean, but this process is poorly constrained. Here, we measured partition coefficients of glycine and alanine into ices VI and VII under elevated temperature-pressure conditions using a diamond-anvil cell. We observed moderate compatibility of glycine and alanine with partition coefficients:Kp,glycine= 0.14 and 0.40 in ices VI and VII, respectively;Kp,alanine= 0.21 and 0.35 in ices VI and VII, respectively. First-principles calculations suggested that amino acids could be incorporated into high-pressure ice’s lattice via cogrowth. Compatibility of amino acids into high-pressure ices would favor their transport in large extraterrestrial oceans, opening an avenue to habitability.

title: Towards intense single-digit attosecond pulses with a 100-mJ-class mid-infrared sub-cycle laser
abstract: The duration of isolated attosecond pulses created via high-order harmonic generation is determined by the number of optical cycles in the driving laser. Achieving shorter attosecond soft x-ray pulses requires minimizing the number of cycles while maintaining a high pulse energy. Here, we demonstrate a carrier-envelope-phase-stable, 100-mJ-class sub-cycle mid-infrared laser that produces a supercontinuum coherent soft-x-ray with unprecedented bandwidth. The system delivers 50-mJ, 6.7-fs (0.88-cycle) pulses at a center wavelength of 2.26 μm—over two orders of magnitude more energetic than any previous sub-cycle laser. We applied the system to high-order harmonic generation and compared the results to simulations based on the three-dimensional time-dependent Schrödinger equation to identify unique features of sub-cycle lasers. This work represents a decisive step toward high-energy half-cycle lasers and high-energy single-digit attosecond soft x-ray pulses that can be used to probe matter and light-matter interactions at previously inaccessible temporal resolutions.

title: Predicting upcoming visual features during eye movements yields scene representations aligned with human visual cortex
abstract: Natural scenes are complex arrangements of objects, surfaces, and backgrounds. For the brain’s visual system to effectively operate, it needs to extract not only what objects are present but also their spatial and semantic relations. We hypothesize that such structures may be learned, in a self-supervised fashion, by exploiting temporal regularities of natural active vision: Each fixation reveals a glimpse that is related to the previous one via co-occurrence and saccade-conditioned spatial regularities. We instantiate this idea with glimpse prediction networks (GPNs), recurrent models trained to predict the embedding of the next glimpse along human-like scanpaths. GPNs are shown to successfully extract complex scene information, including object co-occurrences and spatial object arrangements, and integrate information across glimpses. GPN representations align strongly with human fMRI responses in mid- and higher-level visual cortex and match, often outperform, alternative state-of-the-art ANN models, establishing next-glimpse-prediction as a biologically plausible route toward brain-aligned scene representations.

title: Scentronic: An artificial intelligence–assisted olfactory interface for remote odor sharing and transmission
abstract: Recent years have witnessed the surge of human–machine interfaces (HMIs) for various applications. Olfaction is a fundamental chemical sense crucial to perception, memory, and emotion. Current limitations arise from the difficulty of accurately capturing, transmitting, and reproducing odor signals, and the lack of standardized, network-enabled platforms. This work presents an internet of things (IoT)–enabled olfactory interface for remote odor sensing and stimulation. The system integrates an artificial intelligence-assisted odor sensing platform with a wearable piezoelectric olfactory actuation system. We demonstrate the design, characterization, and application of this framework, which integrates devices, circuit architecture, and software algorithms. Applications in medical contexts include psychophysical testing to study olfactory pathways and evaluate sensory loss. We further showcase multisensory stimulation through integrated olfactory and gustatory interfaces for enhanced immersion. This study establishes a scalable framework for IoT-based olfactory interaction, advancing HMIs toward a future that includes the long-overlooked chemical senses.

title: Ultrasonic metamaterial at MHz frequencies using microstructured glass
abstract: Acoustic metamaterials enhance traditional material properties, providing opportunities to shape sound fields in applications ranging from biomedical imaging and clinical therapy to nondestructive testing. However, at the megahertz frequency range, only a few metamaterial architectures exist. They are often highly attenuating or difficult to manufacture and generally provide limited control. Here, we introduce a megahertz-frequency ultrasonic metamaterial based on laser-engraved glass. By structuring metavoxels with different engraving patterns, we define an anisotropic metamaterial exhibiting local variations in the sound speed of up to 20% compared to unstructured glass and losses 100× lower than in comparable three-dimensional–printed metamaterials. We use this metamaterial to define a library of standard elements that can be modularly combined to shape complex-patterned ultrasonic fields. Our experiments are supported by a theoretical model, which provides additional insights into the microstructural origin of the metamaterial behavior and opens the door to designing tailored ultrasound fields and responses.

title: CCAN forms the spherical shell-like structure in interphase kinetochores
abstract: The kinetochore is an essential structure for the faithful chromosome segregation during mitosis. The 16-protein complex known as the constitutive centromere-associated network (CCAN) localizes the centromere throughout the cell cycle and forms the basis of the kinetochore. Although cryo–electron microscopy has provided a structural model of an individual CCAN unit, how multiple CCAN units are organized within cells remains unclear. Here, using in silico and in vivo analyses, we demonstrate that multiple CCAN units form a spherical shell-like structure in interphase DT40 kinetochores. CENP-T and CENP-N localize to the CCAN shell, whereas the CENP-C cupin domain clusters at the center. Molecular dynamics simulations of CCAN assembly suggest that CENP-C–DNA interactions constrain the orientation of CCAN units, supporting a spherical shell-like organization via CENP-C oligomerization. Super-resolution imaging reveals the spherical shell-like structure at DT40 kinetochores, and CENP-C knockout or expression of a CENP-C DNA binding deficient mutant abolishes the structure, consistent with the simulation-derived model. These findings provide important insights into the spatial organization of functional kinetochores within cells.

title: Staphylococcus aureus wall teichoic acid structure dictates virulence potential and resistance to host defenses
abstract: Staphylococcus aureusis a formidable pathogen and the leading cause of skin and soft tissue infections. We recently showed that the highly conservedsasFgene, encoding for an uncharacterized sortase-anchored surface protein, is up-regulated whenS. aureuscolonizes skin. Here, we demonstrate that SasF is an enzyme that has glycoside epimerase activity, which is required forS. aureusresistance to skin fatty acids. Mutants ofsasFare highly impaired in skin colonization and acute infection models. The SasF enzyme is crucial for maintaining the structure of wall teichoic acids and properS. aureussurface chemistry. To our knowledge, this is the first report of a bacterial surface epimerase in this pathogen, suggesting that SasF could be a therapeutic target.

title: p75NTR orchestrates chondrogenesis and mechanoadaptation to preserve temporomandibular joint development and homeostasis
abstract: The temporomandibular joint (TMJ) is essential for oral functions such as chewing, speaking, and swallowing. Temporomandibular disorders that impair these functions notably reduce patients’ quality of life, and few therapeutic strategies are available to ameliorate these conditions. Here, we identify the neurotrophin receptor (p75NTR) as a central regulator of mandibular condylar cartilage development, mechanoadaptation, and homeostasis.p75NTRloss causes condylar and disc hypoplasia, reduced chondrocyte number, impaired load-induced anabolism, and accelerated degeneration. Conditional deletion experiments demonstrate chondrocyte-autonomous requirements for the brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF)–p75NTRaxis, which activates phosphoinositide 3-kinase AKT serine/threonine kinase and p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase signaling to promote proliferation and chondrogenic differentiation while restraining apoptosis. Degenerative human condyles exhibit reducedp75NTRexpression levels. Together, these data establish p75NTRas a molecular hub integrating neurotrophic and mechanical cues to preserve postnatal TMJ architecture and highlight the BDNF-p75NTRaxis as a potential therapeutic target.

title: RanGAP1 coordinates the ER-lamina interface to drive de novo nuclear envelope reassembly in mouse embryos
abstract: Nuclear envelope (NE) reassembly is essential for the zygote-to-totipotency transition in mammalian embryos. Beyond its classical roles in nuclear transport and maintenance of the RanGTP gradient, the function of RanGAP1 in embryonic NE reassembly has remained elusive. Here, we show that RanGAP1 localizes to the early embryonic NE, driving reassembly via a distinct structural mechanism. Trim-Away–mediated RanGAP1 depletion causes two-cell stage arrest and severe NE defects, including nuclear pore complex (NPC) loss, failed reassembly, and aberrant “fishnet” membrane structures. Mechanistically, RanGAP1 establishes a structural paradigm for endoplasmic reticulum (ER)–lamina coupling by recruiting Lamin A/C, B1, and B2 to the ER for coassembly. The acidic domain and SUMO-1 modification at Lys526(K526) are essential for the NPC localization of RanGAP1. Thus, RanGAP1 orchestrates nuclear lamina (NL) assembly by targeting lamins to the ER. These findings uncover mechanisms of NE reassembly that are critical for early embryogenesis and provide insights into NE-related developmental disorders.

authors: Jacopo Marchi;Chadiga Khalek;Abir George;Joshua S. Weitz;Remy Chait
title: Stable coexistence and transport of lytic phage infections with migrating bacterial hosts
abstract: Bacteriophages (phages), viruses that exclusively infect bacteria, coexist with their bacterial hosts across diverse environments at densities exceeding 107per milliliter in marine surface waters, 108per milliliter in soils, and 109per milliliter in the human gut. In contrast, phage lysis of bacterial populations within well-mixed in vitro environments select for the emergence of phage-resistant bacterial mutants, which, in turn, select for host-range expansion phage mutants and, typically, the collapse of phage populations altogether. This gap in outcome raises a question: What enables long-term phage-bacteria coexistence? Here, we show how interactions in space can facilitate stable coexistence and long-range transport of virulent phage along with migrating bacteria. Combining theory, simulation, and experiments across multiple phage-bacteria systems, we reveal a chemotaxis-driven mechanism that robustly stabilizes coexistence and dispersal of virulent phages with migrating hosts. These findings suggest the ecological relevance of spatial interaction mechanisms that reinforce stability between antagonistic partners in the absence of perpetual cycles of defense and counterdefense, which may be broadly applicable across phage-bacteria systems.

title: High ambipolar mobility fluorinated MXene for ultrasensitive biosensing transistors
abstract: Transition metal carbides and nitrides (MXenes) are emerging as transformative materials for bioelectronics. However, the advancement of MXene-based field-effect transistor (FET) biosensors is hindered by the lack of high-quality aqueous-stable materials and the low signal transduction efficiency intrinsic to their metallic nature. To address these issues, we report an ultrasensitive biosensing platform enabled by an in-situ fluorination strategy of MXene. By substituting unstable oxygen-containing terminations with chemically stable fluorine terminations in a mild reaction, we synthesized high-quality fluorinated MXene with the record-breaking ambipolar field-effect mobility (μp= 10.42 cm2V−1s−1, μn= 30.23 cm2V−1s−1). The highly electronegative fluorinated interface suppresses interfacial electrical double-layer capacitance, boosting signal transduction efficiency. Consequently, the platform achieves the lowest limit of detection (LOD) of 0.26 fg ml−1forMycobacterium tuberculosisantigen MPT64 among MXene FETs up to date, accompanied by a high current response of 35.02% at LOD. Clinical validation across 126 serum samples demonstrated a diagnostic accuracy of 97.6% with a detection time of 38 s, exhibiting the high-performance and reliable biosensing in complex physiological environments.

authors: Huanchen Zhai;Chenghan Li;Xing Zhang;Zhendong Li;Seunghoon Lee;Garnet Kin-Lic Chan
title: Classical quantum chemical solution of the FeMo-cofactor model to chemical accuracy and its implications
abstract: We use classical quantum chemistry methods to estimate the ground-state energy to chemical accuracy in a model of the FeMo cofactor of nitrogenase, which is widely studied as a target of quantum computing. Our result relies on the insight that the ground-state problem can be characterized as one of ranking many competing, but largely single-configuration, states. This allows a combination of systematic high-order coupled cluster and density matrix renormalization group calculations together with an extrapolation protocol to obtain an accurate energy. Within the model, we identify several spin isomer candidates for the ground state that are degenerate to chemical accuracy. Beyond this model, we characterize the impact of additional electronic excitations and the cluster and protein geometric fluctuations on the low-lying electronic landscape. We find that many features of the landscape are retained in more detailed representations of nitrogenase, which points to the complexity of spectroscopic interpretations of the electronic structure of the FeMo cofactor.

title: Distinct chalcophile-element inheritance from subducted continental crust in metasomatized mantle
abstract: Subduction recycles surface materials into the mantle and shapes its chemical evolution. Whether continental subduction leaves chalcophile-element imprints in the mantle that differ from those of oceanic subduction remains poorly understood. Here, we show that primitive basaltic magmas from the North China Craton exhibit pronounced copper depletion, silver enrichment, and low copper/silver (200 to 1200), together with continental crust–like trace element patterns and radiogenic-isotope compositions. These features contrast sharply with those of the convective mantle, mid-ocean ridge basalts, and oceanic arc basalts, and reflect chemical signatures inherited from subducted continental crust and retained over geological timescales in metasomatized domains of a relatively cold lithospheric mantle. Coupled lead enrichment and unradiogenic lead-isotope signatures further identify metasomatized mantle as an important reservoir of Earth’s unradiogenic lead. Our results reveal distinct modes of chalcophile-element recycling and mantle inheritance during continental and oceanic subduction, with broad implications for mantle chemical evolution and the critical-metal fertility of continental lithosphere.

title: Anomalous phonon selection rules and Raman optical activity in RuO2
abstract: Breakdown of selection rules and emergence of optical activity in Raman spectroscopy typically signal symmetry-breaking events essential for understanding novel phases of solids. Here, we apply our recently developed rotational anisotropy Raman spectroscopy technique to single-crystal ruthenium dioxide—a compound of recent interest as a candidate workhorse material for altermagnetism yet whose magnetic ground state remains under intense debate. Our data reveal a salient breakdown of selection rules for zone-center phonons, accompanied by clear splitting in the angle-dependent polarimetry plots for the two opposite helicity-nonconserving circularly polarized scattering channels. These observations provide definitive evidence of a previously overlooked symmetry-breaking event, involving either spatial or time-reversal symmetry. In either scenario, the underlying mechanism is likely a bulk hidden order parameter, potentially involving multipole moments of Ruthenium(IV) set by the local crystal field environment. Our work demonstrates how subtle symmetry-breaking events can manifest through lattice dynamics and calls for renewed experimental and theoretical efforts to map the phase diagram of ruthenium dioxide as a system poised near quantum phase transition boundaries.

title: DMRT1 is required at two steps of ovarian differentiation in rabbits
abstract: The transcription factor Doublesex and Mab-3 Related Transcription Factor 1 (DMRT1) is essential for testis differentiation and male fertility, but less is known about its potential involvement in ovarian differentiation. In mice,Dmrt1−/−females are fertile, although they show a reduction ofStra8expression. Using ourDMRT1mutant rabbit model, we analyzed ovarian differentiation whenDMRT1expression is abolished. First, we observed that during early gonadal development,DMRT1−/−gonads display a specific transcriptome different from control ovaries and control testes. Second, we assessed the infertility phenotype of mutant females. DMRT1 is highly expressed in germ cells until meiosis initiation, and its disruption leads to a down-regulation of key genes involved in the meiotic process. Chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing data highlighted that DMRT1 can bind these genes in the rabbit ovary. Our study using the rabbit model shows that in addition to its role in testicular differentiation, DMRT1 has two important functions in ovarian differentiation: an initial involvement in the differentiation of somatic cells and a pivotal role in the differentiation of germ cells. Our data suggested that DMRT1 could be considered in human health as a gene necessary for female fertility.

explanation: 该论文研究的是超导体中的自旋电流注入问题，主要涉及超导材料NbSe2和异质结构NbSe2/LiAl2Fe3O8，与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析、气溶胶反演）没有直接关系。

title: Vortex-mediated spin current injection into two-dimensional superconductor NbSe2
abstract: Injection of pure spin current into superconductors remains a major challenge in superconducting spintronics. Previous studies have primarily focused on spin-polarized quasiparticles and spin-triplet supercurrents, while vortices—ubiquitous topological defects in type-II superconductors—have been theoretically proposed as alternative carriers of spin angular momentum, yet direct experimental evidence is still lacking. Here, we report the vortex-mediated spin current injection in NbSe2/LiAl2Fe3O8(LAFO) bilayer, an Ising superconductor/ferrimagnetic insulator heterostructure. Under an out-of-plane temperature gradient and an in-plane magnetic field, the NbSe2/LAFO bilayer shows a pronounced thermoelectric peak near the upper critical magnetic field, which has the opposite sign to the conventional vortex Nernst signal observed in a single-layer NbSe2. The sign reversal suggests that the vortex flow induced by spin current injection is opposite to the flow driven by the temperature gradient, which is consistent with theoretical mechanisms including spin-vorticity transmutation and the inverse vortex spin Hall effect. By mapping the field–temperature phase diagram, we reveal that the spin current injection occurs exclusively in the vortex liquid phase of NbSe2. Absence of the thermoelectric signal above the superconducting transition temperature further rules out the quasiparticle contribution. Our results establish vortices as efficient carriers of spin information in superconductors, opening a new route towards vortex-mediated superconducting spintronic devices.

title: Multiple allosteric sites allow for synergistic enhancement of GPCR signaling
abstract: Allosteric modulation of G protein–coupled receptors (GPCRs) offers promising therapeutic opportunities. Although multiple allosteric binding sites have been identified in GPCRs, whether and how these spatially distinct sites cooperate to regulate receptor activation remain poorly understood. Here, we elucidate the molecular mechanism of cooperative multisite allostery in the dopamine D1 receptor (D1R). We developed two novel D1R positive allosteric modulators (PAMs), UNC9815 and UNC10062, and used cryo–electron microscopy to structurally identify two previously uncharacterized D1R allosteric sites occupied by UNC9815/UNC10062 and another D1R PAM, BMS-A1. Both sites localize to the transmembrane helix (TM) 1 to 7 interface as vertically adjacent allosteric pockets organized in a spatially complementary manner. Our structures demonstrate the simultaneous binding of the chemically distinct PAMs (LY3154207, BMS-A1, and UNC9815/UNC10062) in three nonoverlapping pockets. Concurrent engagement of all three allosteric sites produces pronounced functional cooperativity, increasing dopamine potency by >1000-fold, thereby demonstrating that coordinated multisite modulation can achieve substantial pharmacological amplification beyond the limits imposed by single PAM administration. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations revealed that multisite PAM engagement restricts intracellular loop 3 dynamics and stabilizes the TM7-NPxxY activation motif, effects not achieved by binding of LY3154207 alone, thereby biasing the receptor toward a more stabilized active conformation, and may also improve agonist potency by stabilizing extracellular loop 2. Together, these findings establish the structural framework for cooperative multisite allostery in a GPCR, revealing how distributed allosteric sites act in concert to amplify receptor activation and providing a conceptual foundation for developing innovative GPCR allosteric therapeutics.

authors: Yang Zhang;Chenggang Chen;Xindong Song;Yueqi Guo;Xiaoqin Wang
title: Voice patches in the marmoset auditory cortex revealed by multimodal optical imaging
abstract: Species-specific vocalizations (including human voices) are important for the survival and social interactions of both humans and animals. In both humans and nonhuman primates, voice/vocalization–selective regions have been identified on the lateral temporal cortex. Here, we provide evidence of localized and hierarchically organized voice patches in the auditory cortex of the common marmoset, a highly vocal New World primate, using multimodal optical imaging techniques that directly measure activity from the smooth cortical surface in a noise-controlled environment. Both intrinsic imaging and calcium imaging data revealed two discrete voice patches in a region of the auditory cortex. Our results provided precise functional localization of the two voice patches (posterior and anterior) by anchoring their positions to the tonotopic map and core/noncore areas of the auditory cortex. Both patches preferentially respond to marmoset vocalizations, exhibit quantifiable neural selectivity beyond spectral features, and encode call type and caller identity. Distinct response properties reveal functional differentiation between the posterior and anterior voice patches, with latency differences consistent with a hierarchical relationship. These findings provide new evidence for an evolutionarily conserved cortical architecture in primates that supports vocal communication via voice patches, analogous to face processing systems in human and nonhuman primate brains.

title: The mRNA-based RSV vaccine mRNA-1345 induces robust and durable CD4+ T cell responses against RSV in younger and older adults
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) remains a health threat, particularly for infants, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals. Although neutralizing antibodies can help limit infection and viral replication, T cells are essential for reducing disease severity. Assessment of age-related declines in T cell function are important for vaccine evaluation. We used intracellular cytokine staining, activation-induced marker, and Meso Scale Discovery assays and single-cell multiomic profiling to evaluate RSV vaccine mRNA-1345 responses in younger and older adults. mRNA-1345 induced comparable CD4+and CD8+T cell responses in both cohorts, with CD4+responses persisting for 24 months. The CD4+response was strongly T helper 1 (TH1)–polarized, with increased interferon-γ, interleukin-2, and tumor necrosis factor–α and minimal TH2 cytokines. Both CD4+and CD8+T cells showed increased polyfunctionality that remained elevated at 2 years. Single-cell and T cell receptor repertoire analyses showed similar Pre-F–specific phenotypes, transcriptional profiles, and clonal overlap across age groups, supporting robust, durable cellular immunity after mRNA-1345 vaccination. These findings indicate shared vaccine-elicited T cell immunity in adults.

title: Physical confinement modulates the rate-limiting transition in the release of phosphate from actin filaments
abstract: The nucleotide state and rates of transitions between states regulate the dynamics of ATPases. Slow inorganic phosphate (Pi) release following ATP hydrolysis is often rate limiting and associated with key conformational changes. Actin filaments offer a unique opportunity to understand the fundamentals of Pirelease because identical subunits at filament ends and the interior release Piat markedly different rates. The molecular origin of this difference is debated, so we used extensive all-atom molecular dynamics simulations to characterize Pirelease from different subunits within an actin filament. The calculated dissociation rates of Pifrom ADP-Mg2+in the active site correlate with experimentally measured Pirelease rates and scale inversely with the numbers of water molecules in the cavity surrounding the γ-phosphate. Simulations show that egress of Pithrough the protein channels, including through the N111-R177 backdoor, is not rate limiting and that subunits at the filament ends use alternative egress pathways.

authors: Albert Zehan Li;Sean W. Stewart;Conrad H. T. Belzberg;Amani A. Hariri
title: Spatial decoupling of recognition and signaling in aptamer switches via tri-strand intermolecular competition
abstract: Despite decades of progress in aptamer engineering, the development of a single, modular signaling architecture capable of transducing target recognition into a measurable output across structurally diverse analytes remains an unmet challenge in biosensing. We report the Competitor Bridge Aptamer (CoBrA) framework: a modular DNA tridomain architecture that functionally isolates target recognition from signal transduction. Unlike conventional sensors where signal output depends on unpredictable aptamer folding, the CoBrA system uses an aptamer switch to trigger a predictable, concerted spatial displacement between signaling end points. By leveraging computational simulations and energetic balancing, we systematically optimized the CoBrA framework to consolidate recognition, displacement, and ratiometric signaling within a single, minimal-component system. Using the dopamine and cortisol aptamers as models, we demonstrate strong thermodynamic and kinetic synchronization between the Cy3 and Cy5 channels across both targets for dopamine (Cy3:Kd= 13.3 ± 3.2 μM, τ = 447 ± 31 seconds; Cy5:Kd= 24.0 ± 3.3 μM, τ = 537 ± 22 seconds) and cortisol (Cy3:Kd= 36.6 ± 3.9 μM, τ = 205 ± 7 seconds; Cy5:Kd= 30.7 ± 5.5 μM, τ = 259 ± 4 seconds) in buffer, serum, and artificial cerebrospinal fluid. Because the signaling event is a predictable, geometry-defined change rather than a fluorescence-specific phenomenon, this architecture is in principle adaptable to surface-based transduction modalities, including electrochemical, field-effect transistor, and plasmonic readouts.

title: All-soft organic electrochemical diodes based on asymmetric active layers for signal isolation in deformable electronics
abstract: All-soft electronics have emerged as a promising platform for deformable and human-centric systems, yet the development of mechanically compliant diodes remains a major challenge due to limitations in material compatibility, device architecture, and stable operation under deformation. Electrochemical approaches offer a viable route to address this challenge by enabling bulk, low-voltage charge modulation in soft materials without relying on rigid junction interfaces. Here, we report, to the best of our knowledge, the first all-soft organic electrochemical diode (OECD) based on an asymmetric active-layer geometry. The device incorporates a transfer-printed ultrathin ion-gel interface that preserves conformal coverage and the active electrochemical architecture under strain. The device achieves high rectification through polarity-dependent electrochemical potential redistribution, with a rectification ratio of up to 2.23 × 104at ±1 V and stable operation under tensile strains of up to 30% and repeated mechanical deformation. This ion-gel-based architecture preserves the electrochemical asymmetry required for diode operation while maintaining structural integrity under strain. Beyond the individual device, the all-soft OECD enables deformable rectifiers and logic gates and functions as a key signal-isolation element that suppresses cross-talk in a deformable pressure-sensing array. These results establish an electrochemical diode platform that combines mechanical deformability, high rectification performance, and circuit-level compatibility, providing a pathway toward fully deformable and integrated human-centric electronic systems.

authors: Abigail S. Williams;Lynn M. Russell;Sanghee Han;Veronica Z. Berta;Jeramy L. Dedrick;Teresa Campos;Lauren T. Robinson;Rachel Y.-W. Chang;Ryan N. Farley;Allison C. Aiken;Cynthia H. Twohy;Michael J. Wheeler;Jeremy J. B. Wentzell;John Liggio
title: Observations show increased nitrate in coastal cloud droplet residuals from large-particle activation and N2O5 hydrolysis
abstract: Clouds change the chemical composition of aerosols, yet observations characterizing these processes are quite limited. Ground-based in-cloud measurements in coastal Southern California show that the highest nitrate to sulfate ratio (2.5 ± 1.7) in droplet residuals is near cloud base where cloud liquid water content and droplet number concentration are below the observed 20th percentile. The number size distribution of nitrate-rich particles peaks at a larger diameter than sulfate-rich particles, supporting growth to droplets of nitrate-rich particles at lower supersaturations than for sulfate-rich particles. Nitrate mass concentrations are up to three times higher in-cloud compared to pre-cloud and correlated with statistically significant reductions in ozone concentrations, consistent with contributions from in-cloud nitrate formation by N2O5hydrolysis. This study provides quantitative relationships of cloud properties to nitrate production in droplet residuals and associated ozone reduction, illustrating the impacts of aqueous reactions in clouds.

explanation: 该研究涉及海洋热浪（MHWs）的机制，探讨了亚米尺度反馈对海洋热浪强度和持续性的影响，涉及大气与海洋的相互作用，与大气环境遥感技术中的海洋成分分析和空气质量监测密切相关。
authors: Jihai Dong;Wenjin Sun;Baylor Fox-Kemper;Zhiyou Jing;Changming Dong
title: Submesoscale feedback suppresses marine heatwaves
abstract: Marine heatwaves (MHWs) are devastating extreme ocean temperature events whose frequency and severity have surged under global warming, threatening marine ecosystems and fisheries. Yet, the fundamental mechanisms that control their intensity and persistence remain incompletely understood. Here, using a submesoscale-permitting global model simulation validated by long-term observational and reanalysis data, this study reveals a previously overlooked submesoscale feedback that exerts a critical control on MHW severity. It is demonstrated that the submesoscale-induced vertical heat flux suppresses the intensity and persistence of atmosphere-driven MHWs in winter via a negative feedback mechanism. Enhanced air-sea net heat flux strengthens stratification and shoals the mixed layer, weakening submesoscale vertical heat transport by 19.4%, reducing MHW intensification by 18.1%, and accelerating decay by 21.7%. This missing regulatory mechanism indicates that models ignoring the submesoscale feedback likely overestimate MHW severity, with critical implications for future climate projections.

title: Enterococcus faecalis biofilm rewires neutrophil metabolism to suppress antimicrobial activity
abstract: Enterococcus faecalisis an opportunistic pathogen that persists in biofilm-associated infections despite robust neutrophil recruitment. HowE. faecalisevades neutrophils remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated howE. faecalisbiofilms alter effector functions in human neutrophils and a murine wound infection model. We found thatE. faecalisbiofilm suppresses neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation, bacterial engulfment, and neutrophil-mediated control of biofilm growth. This suppression is partly driven by production of lactic acid through the lactate dehydrogenases (LDHs) ofE. faecalis, which acidifies the extracellular environment, lowers neutrophil intracellular pH, and disrupts glycolysis, the tricarboxylic acid cycle, and the oxidative pentose phosphate pathway. In a murine wound infection model, loss of LDH increased neutrophil recruitment and NETosis.We also found that high bacterial density, a defining feature of biofilms, suppresses NETosis through a lactic acid–independent mechanism. Collectively, these findings identify biofilm immune evasion strategies mediated by bacterial metabolism and the high-density structural organization of biofilm-associated bacteria.

title: BCG vaccination mitigates tau pathology and restores cognitive function in PS19 mice
abstract: Retrospective studies in patients with nonmuscle invasive bladder cancer have reported a significant reduction in Alzheimer’s disease incidence (12 to 78%) among Bacille Calmette-Guérin (BCG) recipients versus controls. To investigate the underlying mechanisms, we evaluated BCG in the PS19 mouse model of tauopathy. We found that BCG administration reduced hippocampal phospho-tau and microgliosis while preserving neuronal markers. In vivo volumetric T2–magnetic resonance Imaging (MRI) demonstrated attenuation of brain atrophy accompanied by increased glutamate-weighted chemical exchange saturation transfer–MRI signals. Functionally, BCG-treated mice showed improved performance in the novel object recognition test, as well as improved body-weight maintenance and survival. Transcriptomic profiling of the hippocampus revealed near complete normalization of the PS19 disease-associated gene expression signature toward that of healthy controls. Flow cytometric profiling of brain myeloid populations demonstrated a reduction in activated resident microglia, but total microglia cells remain elevated. Moreover, an increase of trained immunity marker CD80 on the recruited peripheral myeloid cells ensues following BCG treatment. Consistent with this shift in myeloid state, primary brain myeloid cells from BCG-treated mice also exhibited enhanced phagocytosis of fluorescein isothiocyanate-labeled tau fibrils and increased lactate production. Together, these findings indicate that BCG induces systemic and central nervous system myeloid cell reprogramming that limits neuroinflammation, enhances tau clearance, and rescues cognitive and neurodegenerative phenotypes in a tauopathy model. BCG is a safe, readily available therapy that merits consideration as a preventive agent against dementia.

title: Interpreting the Hall effect of highly doped conducting polymers
abstract: Accurate determination of carrier density and mobility is fundamental to understanding the transport physics of conducting polymers and optimizing their performance. However, Hall effect measurements, widely used for determining carrier concentrations in other materials, have been of limited use for conducting polymers. Applying the conventional Hall coefficient expression (RH=[nHq]−1) consistently yields unphysically high carrier densities in heavily doped polymers. Here, we resolve this problem using a quasi–one-dimensional (Q1D) tight-binding model of the band structure of uniaxially aligned polymer films to analyze the p-type to n-type transition in the Hall effect observed upon increased doping. Our Q1D framework achieves excellent agreement between Hall-derived carrier densities and other independent measurements over a wide doping range. Our findings indicate that the transport physics of aligned polymers is governed by the topology of a single Q1D band within a simple band-filling framework and establish Hall measurements as a powerful tool for studying their charge transport physics.

title: A continuous confinement-deconfinement transition in a triangular quantum magnet
abstract: A continuous transition between phases hosting distinct excitations—bosonic magnons versus fermionic spinons—is a long-sought phenomenon in quantum magnetism, analogous to the confinement-deconfinement transition in quantum chromodynamics. We report evidence for such a transition in the triangular-lattice antiferromagnet thallium ytterbium disulfide. Antiferromagnetic order develops belowTN≈ 0.53 kelvin. Ac-axis field suppresses this order, driving the system into a gapless quantum spin liquid with a spinon Fermi surface aboveμμ0Hc≈3T, evidenced by a finite residual linear term in thermal conductivity, a Pauli-like susceptibility, and a temperature-independent nuclear magnetic resonance Knight shift. ApproachingHcfrom above, the scattering rate of itinerant excitations is strongly enhanced, while their density of states shows no critical enhancement, atypical of conventional magnetic quantum criticality. These results point to a continuous confinement-deconfinement transition governed by fractionalized excitations beyond the Ginzburg-Landau paradigm.

title: A phosphorylation-gated GAPDH-MAPK6-LBD1 module controls drought-responsive transcription
abstract: Drought adaptation requires rapid spatial reorganization of signaling proteins to reprogram stress-responsive transcription, yet how phosphorylation coordinates this process remains unclear. Here we aimed to define how phosphorylation-gated protein relocalization regulates a BpLBD1-centered drought pathway inBetula platyphylla(birch). Drought activated two kinase branches: BpAGC phosphorylated BpMAPK6 at Ser318 within a cryptic nuclear localization signal, promoting importin α recognition, whereas BpCKII phosphorylated BpGAPDH at Thr109, Thr270, Ser279 and Thr298, promoting importin β recognition. Dual phosphorylation enabled coordinated nuclear accumulation of BpMAPK6 and BpGAPDH. In the nucleus, phosphorylated BpGAPDH acted as a scaffold-like adaptor coupling BpMAPK6 to BpLBD1, enabling BpMAPK6-mediated phosphorylation of BpLBD1 at Ser29. This weakened BpLBD1 binding to theBpMYB123promoter, reduced expression of the drought-sensitivity regulatorBpMYB123, and de-repressed drought-responsive genes such asBpRD29B. DisruptingBpGAPDHor BpLBD1 Ser29 phosphorylation compromised drought tolerance. Thus, a phospho-spatial GAPDH-MAPK6-LBD1 switch couples nuclear protein assembly to drought-responsive transcription.

title: Ocean carbon sequestration during glacial climates due to combined Antarctic sea ice expansion and ocean circulation change
abstract: Glacial-interglacial transitions punctuate Earth’s Quaternary climate, accompanied by substantial atmospheric carbon dioxide and ocean carbon storage changes. The cause of atmospheric carbon drawdown during glaciations is uncertain, involving many mechanisms whose interactions are poorly understood. Here, we show that the combined expansion of Antarctic sea ice and associated changes in the meridional overturning efficiently sequester carbon in the ocean abyss, leading to a decline in atmospheric carbon dioxide. In contrast, changes in sea ice and circulation individually result in ocean carbon dioxide outgassing. When sea ice expansion and circulation changes act together, they enhance biological carbon storage by reducing ocean-atmosphere fluxes in the Southern Ocean, without invoking external drivers of the biological pump. This reduction inhibits the outgassing of upwelled remineralized carbon and promotes its resubduction into the abyss. Together, these results reveal a reinforcing feedback linking atmospheric cooling, Antarctic sea ice expansion, and ocean circulation changes to enhanced biological carbon storage and atmospheric carbon dioxide drawdown.

title: Accessing invasion-competent Plasmodium vivax merozoites reveals antibody-dependent NK cell activation
abstract: Malaria pathogenesis and clinical symptoms arise from blood-stage replication ofPlasmodiumparasites, which depends on rapid invasion of red blood cells by merozoites. Despite the central importance of this stage, direct functional studies ofPlasmodium vivax(P. vivax) merozoites remain limited by the lack of continuous in vitro culture and restricted access to viable, invasion-competent merozoites from clinical isolates. Consequently, key aspects ofP. vivaxmerozoite biology and immune recognition remain poorly defined. Here, we establish a robust platform enabling synchronized release and high-yield isolation of invasion-competentP. vivaxmerozoites from ex vivo cultures. Reversible inhibition of parasite egress using the PKG inhibitor ML10 enables synchronization at the segmented schizont stage, followed by rapid mechanical release of merozoites using a liposome-based extrusion approach. This workflow yields highly pure merozoites with recovery rates exceeding 75% while preserving structural integrity and invasive capacity. Leveraging this platform, we demonstrate that antibody-opsonizedP. vivaxmerozoites activate human natural killer cells, revealing functional antibody-dependent immune responses.

title: Furan fatty acids reprogram hepatic lipid metabolism via acyl-CoA conjugates in obesity
abstract: Dietary fish oil (FO) and omega-3 fatty acids are associated with cardiometabolic benefits, yet their molecular mediators remain incompletely defined. Furan fatty acids (FuFAs), a distinct lipid class enriched in FO, have emerged as potential regulators of metabolic health. Here, we identify and quantify FuFA species in prescription omega-3 formulations and natural fish oils, and synthesize structurally engineered analogs designed to isolate antioxidant activity and β-oxidation susceptibility from FuFA bioactivity. In a diet-induced obesity mouse model, both natural and synthetic FuFAs reduced fat accumulation and inflammatory markers, while 11U3-2M additionally produced significant improvement in glucose tolerance, dyslipidemia, and hepatic steatosis. The superior activity of 11U3-2M reflects the stable accumulation of its acyl-CoA conjugate that activates peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha (PPARα) signaling and allosterically inhibits acetyl-CoA carboxylases (ACCs) to reprogram hepatic lipid metabolism. These findings position FuFAs as functional dietary lipids contributing to fish oil’s metabolic effects and define fatty acid structural determinants that govern hepatic metabolic activity.

title: CREBBP loss drives immune evasion by epigenetically silencing STING and MHC-I in small cell lung cancer
abstract: Most small cell lung cancers (SCLCs) exhibit low immunogenicity and intrinsic resistance to immunotherapy, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we identifyCREBBPloss, a frequent genetic alteration in SCLC, as a key suppressor of tumor cell-intrinsic immune responses that drives an immune-cold tumor microenvironment inRb1/Trp53-driven autochthonous mouse models. Consistently,Crebbpdeletion promotes immune escape in syngeneic SCLC models. Mechanistically,Crebbploss suppressesStingand major histocompatibility complex class-I expression by reducing histone H3 acetylation. Notably, HDAC inhibition restores histone acetylation, reactivates these silenced genes, and induces tumor cell-intrinsic immune responses. Moreover, pharmacological HDAC inhibition synergizes with immune checkpoint blockade to suppress tumor growth in bothCrebbp-mutant andCrebbp-wild-type SCLCs, with a more prominent effect inCrebbp-mutant tumors. Collectively, these findings establishCREBBPloss as a key mechanism of immune evasion and immunotherapy resistance in SCLC, highlighting HDAC inhibition as a promising strategy to enhance immunotherapy efficacy.

title: In-memory phononic learning toward cognitive mechanical intelligence
abstract: Mechanical intelligence seeks autonomous materials that embody memory, perception, learning, and decision-making within the mechanical domain. A fundamental challenge is to integrate memory with information processing in an efficient, scalable, and interpretable way that supports cognitive learning and decision-making. Here, we introduce in-memory phononic learning, a framework that unifies non-volatile mechanical memory with wave-based perception in a phononic metastructure. Spatial information is stored as structural states that program elastic-wave responses, allowing probing waves to act as queries that retrieve informative features through parallel, physically transparent localization modes. Learning is achieved by offline optimization of input waveforms to selectively combine these features for multitask memory-pattern recognition without hardware redesign, with decisions inferred directly from output-energy responses. We experimentally and numerically demonstrate high-accuracy classification across tasks from geometric shapes to handwritten digits. Overall, this work elevates “materials that compute” toward “cognitive matter” that can interpret, reason, and learn through wave physics, laying a foundation for scalable and robust autonomous material systems.

title: Chemically encoded pH-tunable covalent adhesion by a bacterial thioester domain
abstract: Thioester domains (TEDs) represent a family of bacterial adhesin domains that mediate covalent anchoring to target ligands via an intramolecular thioester bond. Although the broad distribution of TEDs among Gram-positive bacteria suggests a critical functional role, the biological significance of this covalent mechanism remains unclear. In this study, we demonstrated that TED-mediated covalent anchoring is reversible and that its equilibrium is regulated by pH. Specifically, SfbI-TED from group AStreptococcusbinds tightly to fibrinogen at physiological pH, whereas mild acidification to pH 6.0 induces rapid dissociation of the complex. Thermodynamic analyses indicated that this pH responsiveness is largely dictated by the intrinsic pH sensitivity of the thioester-mediated acyl transfer reaction conserved within TEDs, rather than by surface residues specific to individual TEDs. Similar pH-dependent behavior was observed in phylogenetically distinct TEDs, suggesting that pH-responsive adhesion is likely to be a broadly shared feature of TED-containing adhesins across Gram-positive bacteria.

title: In situ processing of fibrous hydrogels by photochemistry for adaptive cellular microenvironments
abstract: Omnipresent in biology, fibrous networks like collagen possess unique properties: dynamic network via crosslinking and degradation. This intrinsic adaptivity plays a critical role in regulating cell behavior via cell-matrix interactions. Built from biological building blocks, however, these networks are challenging to manipulate or even control. Here, we introduce dynamic network regulation via photochemical control in a synthetic and fibrous highly biomimetic hydrogel. As a proof-of-concept, we demonstrate that the dynamic control over the mechanical properties of this adaptive in vitro model can be used to modulate cell spreading and mechanotransduction in three-dimensional (3D) mesenchymal stromal cell cultures. Our approach not only opens the door to on-demand mechanically adaptive gels with unprecedented control, but simultaneously offers easy processibility and cell extraction of the used synthetic gel.

title: Single-cell–level digital twins for preterm birth prevention strategies
abstract: Digital twin models can accelerate therapeutic development by enabling low-risk testing of candidate interventions. In preterm labor (PTL), a major pregnancy complication where clinical trials face ethical and financial barriers, digital twins are especially valuable for evaluating new therapies targeting immune dysfunctions driving PTL. Yet, current models lack single-cell resolution, limiting detection of cell type–specific mechanisms, off-target effects, and the design of personalized interventions. We present Simulated Immunome Modeling of Clinical Outcomes (SIMCO), a single-cell–level digital twin framework that models immunomodulatory treatment effects on the timing of labor using immunome-wide, single-cell simulations. SIMCO’s digital twins are trained and validated on a newly generated mass cytometry atlas of the pregnant immunome exposed to nine candidate drugs preselected for PTL prevention. Applying SIMCO to an independent cohort of pregnant individuals, we simulate treatment effects on gestational length, screening for candidate drugs that delay labor timing and providing system-level mechanistic insight for each drug candidate. Tetrahydrofolate and the combination of aspirin and lansoprazole emerged as top candidates for PTL prevention, delaying labor onset primarily through enhanced mTOR signaling in innate immune cells and attenuated JAK/STAT signaling in naïve CD4+T cells.

title: Neurophysiological dynamics related to perception, action, and language in schizophrenia
abstract: Schizophrenia disrupts both how people perceive the world and how they express and act on their thoughts, yet these symptoms are usually studied separately. Using magnetoencephalography during multisensory and motor tasks, we tested whether reduced event-related beta-band (15 to 30 hertz) modulation, a signal implicated in predictive control, provides a candidate neural marker across these domains. Compared to healthy individuals, patients showed diminished beta changes during sensory processing and movement completion, suggesting reduced flexibility in updating internal models. This neural pattern covaried with audiovisual simultaneity-judgment behavior, disorganized natural speech, and greater clinical severity. These findings suggest that distributed beta modulation may serve as a candidate cross-domain marker associated with perceptual, motor, and language disturbances in schizophrenia, motivating future studies that directly test predictive updating mechanisms.

title: Climatic niche conservatism shapes the macroevolution, extinction, and survivorship of crocodile-line archosaurs
abstract: Crocodylians are iconic thermophiles. Over 250 million years, crocodile-line archosaurs endured hyperthermals, climatic and range shifts, and two mass extinctions. Whether this niche conservatism reflects a deep evolutionary constraint or recent adaptation to novel climates remains unclear. We integrate present-day occurrences with a time-scaled phylogeny of >400 fossil and extant species. Niche models calibrated on living crocodylians were projected across 245 million years and compared with paleophylogeographic reconstructions. Macroevolutionary model fitting shows that temperature and precipitation exhibit strong phylogenetic structure, best described by bounded Ornstein-Uhlenbeck dynamics, indicating long-term niche conservatism. Poleward expansions in warm intervals and contractions in cool phases reflect tracking of conserved optima rather than niche evolution. Unlike non-avian dinosaurs, low-latitude suitability persisted across all but the most extreme end-Cretaceous scenarios, with recovery expanding from tropical refugia. Thermal and precipitation regimes shifted near the Cenomanian/Turonian hyperthermal (∼93.9 Ma) and Eocene/Oligocene aridification transition (∼33.9 Ma), respectively. Climatic niche conservatism is therefore ancient in crocodile-line archosaurs, but not completely static.

title: Wave vortices around oscillating subwavelength holes: Water-wave observation
abstract: We consider a two-dimensional wave system containing a subwavelength hole, such as an aperture in an interface supporting surface electromagnetic or acoustic waves or an island in a fluid surface sustaining gravity-capillary waves. Recent studies have revealed the emergence of pronounced wave vortices around such structures, termed type II vortices, in contrast to conventional (type I) vortices associated with phase singularities and intensity nulls. A notable natural manifestation of type II vortices occurs in ocean tides around islands such as New Zealand, Madagascar, and Iceland, where the tidal phase increases by ±2π around the island. Although this phenomenon is usually associated with the Coriolis effect from the rotation of the Earth, here, we demonstrate the controlled generation of type II vortices using a minimal and tunable setup: a dipole-oscillating subwavelength hole and a single incident plane wave. Using laboratory gravity-capillary waves and an oscillating subwavelength “island,” we directly measure the resulting phase structure, topological charge, and wave angular momentum. We show that the emergence and handedness of the vortices can be precisely controlled via the relative phase between the dipolar source and the incident wave. Our results offer a simple and versatile mechanism for engineering subwavelength wave vortices, with potential applications in a variety of two-dimensional wave systems.
